title.zh: 卷四十七 列傳第三十七 荀伯玉 崔祖思 蘇侃 虞悰 胡諧之 虞玩之 劉休 江祏
title.en: Volume 47 Biographies 37: Xun Boyu, Cui Zusi, Su Kan, Yu Cong, Hu Xiezhi, Yu Wanzhi, Liu Xiu, Jiang Shi
title.raw: 卷四十七 列傳第三十七 荀伯玉 崔祖思 蘇侃 虞悰 胡諧之 虞玩之 劉休 江祏 Volume 47 Biographies 37: Xun Boyu, Cui Zusi, Su Kan, Yu Cong, Hu Xiezhi, Yu Wanzhi, Liu Xiu, Jiang Shi

sentences.zh: 荀伯玉

translations.literal: Xun Boyu
translations.idiomatic: Xun Boyu

sentences.zh: 齊高帝鎮淮陰，伯玉為高帝冠軍刑獄參軍。

translations.literal: When the Qi Emperor Gao was garrisoned at Huaiyin, Boyu served as the Champion General's Punishments and Prisons Attendant for the Emperor Gao.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Gao of Qi held Huaiyin, Xun Boyu served him as Attendant in the Champion General's office for punishments and prisons.

sentences.zh: 高帝為宋明帝所疑，被徵為黃門郎，深懷憂慮，見平澤有群鶴，仍命筆詠之曰：「八風舞遙翮，九野弄清音，一摧雲間志，為君苑中禽。」

translations.literal: The Emperor Gao was suspected by Emperor Ming of Song and was summoned to serve as Huangmen Lang. Deep in worry, he saw a flock of cranes on the level marsh and straightway ordered a brush to compose verse, saying: "The eight winds dance distant pinions, the nine wilds play clear tones; once the ambition amid the clouds is shattered, one becomes a park bird for his lord."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao fell under suspicion from Emperor Ming of Song and was recalled to the capital as Gentleman at the Yellow Gate. Deeply troubled, he saw a flock of cranes on the flat marshlands and at once took up his brush to write: "The eight winds stir distant wings, the nine realms ring with clear song; crush the will that soared among the clouds, and you become a caged bird in his park.

sentences.zh: 以示伯玉深指，伯玉勸高帝遣數十騎入魏界，安置標榜。

translations.literal: He showed it to Boyu as a profound hint; Boyu urged the Emperor Gao to send several dozen horsemen into Wei territory to set up boundary markers.
translations.idiomatic: He showed the poem to Boyu as a pointed message. Boyu urged the emperor to send several dozen riders into Wei territory to erect boundary markers.

sentences.zh: 魏果遣遊騎數百履行界上，高帝以聞。

translations.literal: Wei indeed sent several hundred patrol riders to traverse the border, and the Emperor Gao reported this.
translations.idiomatic: Wei duly sent hundreds of patrol horsemen to ride the frontier, and Emperor Gao reported this to the court.

sentences.zh: 猶懼不得留，令伯玉占。

translations.literal: Still fearing he would not be allowed to remain, he had Boyu divine.
translations.idiomatic: Still afraid he would not be permitted to stay, he had Boyu cast a divination.

sentences.zh: 伯玉言不成行，而帝卒復本任。

translations.literal: Boyu said the journey would not come to pass, and the Emperor in the end was restored to his original post.
translations.idiomatic: Boyu foretold that the journey would not take place, and the emperor was ultimately returned to his former post.

sentences.zh: 由是見親待。

translations.literal: From this he was treated with intimacy and favor.
translations.idiomatic: From that time he was treated with personal favor.

sentences.zh: 高帝有故吏東莞竺景秀嘗以過系作部，高帝謂伯玉：「卿比看景秀不？」

translations.literal: The Emperor Gao had a former subordinate, Zhuge Jingxiu of Dongguan, who had once been detained in the work department for an offense. The Emperor Gao said to Boyu: "Have you lately looked in on Jingxiu?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao had a former clerk, Zhuge Jingxiu of Dongguan, who had once been held in the labor office for an offense. The emperor asked Boyu, "Have you looked in on Jingxiu lately?

sentences.zh: 答曰：「數往候之，備加責誚，云'若許某自新，必吞刀刮腸，飲灰洗胃'。」

translations.literal: He replied: "I have gone many times to visit him and reproached him fully, saying, 'If you grant me to renew myself, I shall surely swallow a blade and scrape my bowels, drink ash and wash my stomach.'"
translations.idiomatic: Boyu answered, "I have visited him repeatedly and rebuked him thoroughly, saying, 'If you allow me to reform, I will swallow a knife and scour my bowels, drink ashes and wash out my stomach.'"

sentences.zh: 帝善其答，即釋之，卒為忠信士。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved his answer and immediately released him; he in the end became a loyal and faithful man.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his reply and at once released Jingxiu, who in the end proved a loyal and trustworthy man.

sentences.zh: 後隨高帝還都，除奉朝請。

translations.literal: Later he followed the Emperor Gao back to the capital and was appointed Fengchao Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Later he followed Emperor Gao back to the capital and was appointed Attendant at Court.

sentences.zh: 高帝使主家事。

translations.literal: The Emperor Gao had him oversee household affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao put him in charge of household affairs.

sentences.zh: 武帝罷廣興還，立別宅，遣人於大宅掘樹數株，伯玉不與，馳以聞。

translations.literal: The Emperor Wu closed Guangxing and returned, established a separate residence, and sent men to dig up several trees from the great mansion; Boyu would not permit it and rushed to report it.
translations.idiomatic: When the future Emperor Wu closed Guangxing and returned, he set up a separate residence and sent men to dig up several trees from the main mansion; Boyu refused permission and rushed to report it.

sentences.zh: 高帝善之。

translations.literal: The Emperor Gao commended this.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao approved of this.

sentences.zh: 高帝為南兗州，伯玉從轉鎮軍中兵參軍，帶廣陵令。

translations.literal: When the Emperor Gao was [governor of] Nan Yanzhou, Boyu followed him and was transferred to Staff Officer for Central Troops in the Frontier Army, concurrently serving as Magistrate of Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gao held Nan Yan Province, Boyu followed him and was transferred to Staff Officer for Central Troops in the Frontier Army, with concurrent appointment as Magistrate of Guangling.

sentences.zh: 初，高帝在淮陰，伯玉假還廣陵，夢上廣陵城南樓，上有二青衣小兒語伯玉云：「草中肅，九五相追逐。」

translations.literal: Initially, when the Emperor Gao was at Huaiyin, Boyu took leave to return to Guangling and dreamed of ascending the south tower of Guangling city; atop it two boys in blue robes said to Boyu: "Amid the grass, su; nine-five pursue one another."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Emperor Gao was at Huaiyin, Boyu took leave to return to Guangling and dreamed he climbed the south tower of Guangling. Two boys in blue robes said to him, "Amid the grass, su; nine-five pursue one another.

sentences.zh: 伯玉視城下人頭皆有草。

translations.literal: Boyu looked and saw that all the heads of people below the city had grass on them.
translations.idiomatic: Boyu looked down and saw that every head in the city below had grass on it.

sentences.zh: 泰始七年，又夢高帝乘船在廣陵北渚，兩腋下有翅不舒。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Taishi, he again dreamed that the Emperor Gao was boating at the north ford of Guangling, with wings under both armpits that would not spread.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Taishi he dreamed again that Emperor Gao was boating at the north ford of Guangling, with wings under both armpits that would not unfold.

sentences.zh: 伯玉問何當舒，帝曰：「卻後三年。」

translations.literal: Boyu asked when they would spread; the Emperor said: "After three more years."
translations.idiomatic: Boyu asked when they would spread. The emperor said, "In three more years.

sentences.zh: 伯玉夢中自謂是咒師，凡六唾咒之，有六龍出，兩腋下翅皆舒，還復斂。

translations.literal: In the dream Boyu took himself to be an incantation master; altogether six times he spat incantations, and six dragons emerged; the wings under both armpits all spread, then drew in again.
translations.idiomatic: In the dream Boyu took himself to be a spell-master. Six times he spat incantations; six dragons appeared, the wings under both armpits spread fully, then folded back again.

sentences.zh: 元徽二年，而高帝破桂陽，威名大震，五年而廢蒼梧，謂伯玉曰：「卿夢今且效矣。」

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanhui, the Emperor Gao defeated Guiyang and his martial renown greatly shook; in the fifth year he deposed Cangwu and said to Boyu: "Your dream is about to take effect now."
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yuanhui Emperor Gao defeated Guiyang and his martial renown shook the realm; in the fifth year he deposed Emperor Cangwu and told Boyu, "Your dream is about to come true."

sentences.zh: 時武帝在東宮，自以年長，與高帝同創大業，朝事大小悉皆專斷，多違制度。

translations.literal: At that time the Emperor Wu was in the Eastern Palace; considering himself older and having founded the great enterprise together with the Emperor Gao, he decided all court matters large and small on his own, often violating regulations.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the future Emperor Wu was in the Eastern Palace. Considering himself the elder and a co-founder of the great enterprise with Emperor Gao, he decided all court affairs large and small on his own, often in violation of regulations.

sentences.zh: 左右張景真偏見任遇，又多僭侈。

translations.literal: His attendant Zhang Jingzhen was shown partial favor and trust, and was moreover extravagant beyond his station.
translations.idiomatic: His favorite Zhang Jingzhen enjoyed undue favor and trust, and was moreover extravagant beyond his station.

sentences.zh: 武帝拜陵還，景真白服乘畫舴艋，坐胡床。

translations.literal: When the Emperor Wu returned from paying respects at the tombs, Jingzhen wore white dress, rode a painted skiff, and sat on a folding camp chair.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince returned from paying respects at the tombs, Jingzhen wore white dress, rode a painted skiff, and sat on a folding camp chair.

sentences.zh: 觀者咸疑是太子，內外祗畏，莫敢有言者。

translations.literal: Onlookers all suspected he was the crown prince; inside and outside all showed reverent awe, and none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: Onlookers all took him for the crown prince. Inside and outside the palace all showed reverent awe, and none dared speak up.

sentences.zh: 驍騎將軍陳胤叔先已陳景真及太子前後得失，伯玉因武帝拜陵之後，密啟之，上大怒。

translations.literal: The Valiant Cavalry General Chen Yinshu had already reported Jingzhen's and the crown prince's merits and faults before and after; Boyu, taking advantage of the time after the Emperor Wu paid respects at the tombs, secretly memorialized about this, and the sovereign was greatly enraged.
translations.idiomatic: Valiant Cavalry General Chen Yinshu had already reported on Jingzhen and the crown prince's conduct. After the crown prince returned from the tombs, Boyu secretly memorialized the emperor, who flew into a rage.

sentences.zh: 豫章王嶷素有寵，政以武帝長嫡，又南郡王兄弟並列，故武帝為太子，至是有改易之意。

translations.literal: Prince of Yuzhang, Xiao Ye, had long enjoyed favor; it was only because the Emperor Wu was the eldest legitimate son and the Prince of Nanjun's brothers stood equal that the Emperor Wu was made crown prince—now there arose intent to change this.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiao Ye of Yuzhang had long enjoyed favor. Only because the crown prince was the eldest legitimate son and the Prince of Nanjun's brothers stood on equal footing had he been named heir; now the emperor considered replacing him.

sentences.zh: 武帝東還，遣文惠太子、聞喜公子良宣敕詰責，並示以景真罪狀，使以太子令收景真殺之。

translations.literal: When the Emperor Wu returned east, he sent the Wenhui crown prince and the Prince of Wenxi, Zi Liang, to proclaim the edict rebuking him, and also showed the charges against Jingzhen, ordering them to arrest Jingzhen by crown prince command and execute him.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince returned east, the emperor sent the Wenhui crown prince and Prince Zi Liang of Wenxi to proclaim an edict of rebuke, showed them Jingzhen's offenses, and ordered them to arrest and execute Jingzhen by crown prince command.

sentences.zh: 胤叔因白武帝，皆言伯玉以聞。

translations.literal: Yinshu thereupon informed the Emperor Wu; all said it was Boyu who had reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Yinshu then informed the crown prince; everyone said it was Boyu who had reported it.

sentences.zh: 武帝憂懼，稱疾月餘日。

translations.literal: The Emperor Wu was anxious and fearful, and claimed illness for more than a month.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince was anxious and fearful and claimed illness for more than a month.

sentences.zh: 上怒不解，晝臥太陽殿，王敬則直入叩頭，啟請往東宮以慰太子。

translations.literal: The sovereign's anger did not subside; he lay down by day in the Taiyang Hall. Wang Jingze entered straightway, kowtowed, and memorialized asking to go to the Eastern Palace to console the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's anger did not subside. He lay down by day in the Taiyang Hall. Wang Jingze entered straightway, kowtowed, and asked permission to go to the Eastern Palace to console the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 高帝無言，敬則因大聲宣旨往東宮，命裝束。

translations.literal: The Emperor Gao said nothing; Jingze thereupon proclaimed the edict aloud to go to the Eastern Palace and ordered preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao said nothing. Jingze thereupon proclaimed aloud the edict to go to the Eastern Palace and ordered preparations made.

sentences.zh: 又敕太官設饌，密遣人報武帝，令奉迎。

translations.literal: He also ordered the Imperial Kitchen to set out a feast and secretly sent someone to inform the Emperor Wu, ordering him to come forth to receive him.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered the Imperial Kitchen to set out a feast and secretly sent word to the crown prince to come forth and receive him.

sentences.zh: 因呼左右索輿，高帝了無動意。

translations.literal: He then called to his attendants to fetch the carriage; the Emperor Gao showed not the slightest intent to move.
translations.idiomatic: He then called to his attendants to fetch the carriage, but Emperor Gao showed not the slightest intent to move.

sentences.zh: 敬則索衣以衣高帝，仍牽上輿。

translations.literal: Jingze fetched clothes and dressed the Emperor Gao, then still pulled him onto the carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Jingze fetched clothes and dressed the emperor, then pulled him onto the carriage.

sentences.zh: 遂幸東宮，召諸王宴飲，因游玄圃園。

translations.literal: He then visited the Eastern Palace, summoned the princes to feast and drink, and proceeded to stroll in the Xuanyuan Garden.
translations.idiomatic: He then visited the Eastern Palace, summoned the princes to feast and drink, and strolled in the Xuanyuan Garden.

sentences.zh: 長沙王晃捉華蓋，臨川王映執雉尾扇，聞喜公子良持酒槍，南郡王行酒，武帝與豫章王嶷及敬則自捧肴饌。

translations.literal: The Prince of Changsha, Huang, held the ceremonial canopy; the Prince of Linchuan, Ying, held the pheasant-tail fan; the Prince of Wenxi, Zi Liang, held the wine ladle; the Prince of Nanjun poured wine; the Emperor Wu and the Prince of Yuzhang, Ye, and Jingze personally presented dishes.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Huang of Changsha held the ceremonial canopy; Prince Ying of Linchuan held the pheasant-tail fan; Prince Zi Liang of Wenxi held the wine ladle; the Prince of Nanjun poured wine; the crown prince and Prince Ye of Yuzhang and Jingze personally presented the dishes.

sentences.zh: 高帝大飲，賜武帝以下酒，並大醉盡歡，日暮乃去。

translations.literal: The Emperor Gao drank heavily, bestowed wine on the Emperor Wu and those below, and all became greatly drunk in full merriment; only at dusk did they leave.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao drank heavily, bestowed wine on the crown prince and those below, and all became greatly drunk in full merriment; only at dusk did they leave.

sentences.zh: 是日微敬則，則東宮殆廢。

translations.literal: Had it not been for Jingze that day, the Eastern Palace would nearly have been abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Had it not been for Jingze that day, the Eastern Palace would nearly have been abolished.

sentences.zh: 高帝重伯玉盡心，愈見信任，使掌軍國密事，權動朝右。

translations.literal: The Emperor Gao valued Boyu's wholehearted devotion and trusted him ever more, putting him in charge of secret military and state affairs; his power moved the right side of court.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao valued Boyu's wholehearted devotion and trusted him ever more, putting him in charge of secret military and state affairs; his power moved the right side of court.

sentences.zh: 每暫休外，軒蓋填門。

translations.literal: Whenever he briefly rested outside [office], carriage canopies filled his gate.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he briefly rested outside office, carriage canopies filled his gate.

sentences.zh: 嘗遭母憂，成服日，左率蕭景先、侍中王晏共載吊之。

translations.literal: He once suffered his mother's mourning; on the day he completed mourning dress, the Left Commander Xiao Jingxian and the Attendant-in-Ordinary Wang Yan rode together to offer condolences.
translations.idiomatic: When he suffered his mother's mourning, on the day he completed mourning dress Left Commander Xiao Jingxian and Attendant-in-Ordinary Wang Yan rode together to offer condolences.

sentences.zh: 五更便巾車，未到伯玉宅二里許，王侯朝士已盈巷，至下鼓尚未得前，司徒褚彥回、衛軍王儉俱進繼後方得前，又倚聽事久之。

translations.literal: At the fifth watch they set out in a covered carriage; before reaching within about two li of Boyu's residence, princes and court gentlemen already filled the lane; by the time of the evening drum they still had not been able to advance. The Minister of Works Chu Yanhui and the Defender-in-Chief Wang Jian both pressed forward in succession behind others before they could advance, and leaned on the reception hall a long while.
translations.idiomatic: At the fifth watch they set out in a covered carriage. Before they were within about two li of Boyu's residence, princes and court gentlemen already filled the lane. By the evening drum they still had not been able to advance. Minister of Works Chu Yanhui and Defender-in-Chief Wang Jian both pressed forward in succession behind others before they could advance, and leaned on the reception hall a long while.

sentences.zh: 中詔遣中書舍人徐希秀斷哭止客，久方得吊。

translations.literal: A central edict sent the Secretariat Gentleman Xu Xixiu to cut off weeping and stop visitors; only after a long while could they offer condolences.
translations.idiomatic: A central edict sent Secretariat Gentleman Xu Xixiu to cut off weeping and stop visitors; only after a long while could they offer condolences.

sentences.zh: 比出，二人饑乏，氣息惙然，切齒形於聲貌。

translations.literal: By the time they came out, the two men were hungry and exhausted, their breath faint; grinding their teeth showed in voice and countenance.
translations.idiomatic: By the time they came out, the two men were hungry and exhausted, their breath faint; grinding their teeth showed in voice and countenance.

sentences.zh: 明日入宮，言便云：「臣等所見二宮門及齋合方荀伯玉宅，政可設雀羅。」

translations.literal: The next day they entered the palace and at once said: "What we saw—the two palace gates and the fasting hall were just Xun Boyu's residence; one might as well set up a net for sparrows."
translations.idiomatic: The next day they entered the palace and at once said, "What we saw—the two palace gates and the fasting hall were just Xun Boyu's residence; one might as well set up a net for sparrows.

sentences.zh: 續復言：「外論云，千敕萬令，不如荀公一命。」

translations.literal: They went on to say: "Outside it is said, a thousand edicts and ten thousand orders are not equal to one word from Lord Xun."
translations.idiomatic: They went on, "Outside it is said, a thousand edicts and ten thousand orders are not equal to one word from Lord Xun."

sentences.zh: 武帝深怨伯玉，高帝臨崩，指伯玉以屬武帝。

translations.literal: The Emperor Wu deeply resented Boyu; as the Emperor Gao lay dying, he pointed to Boyu and entrusted him to the Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu deeply resented Boyu. As Emperor Gao lay dying, he pointed to Boyu and entrusted him to Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: 武帝即位，伯玉憂懼。

translations.literal: When the Emperor Wu took the throne, Boyu was anxious and fearful.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu took the throne, Boyu was anxious and fearful.

sentences.zh: 上聞之，以其與垣崇祖善，崇祖田業在江西，慮相扇為亂，加意撫之，伯玉乃安。

translations.literal: The sovereign heard of this; because he was on good terms with Yuan Chongzu, and Chongzu's fields and estates were in Jiangxi, fearing they might incite each other to rebellion, he showed special care in comforting him, and Boyu then was at ease.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard of this. Because Boyu was on good terms with Yuan Chongzu, whose fields and estates lay in Jiangxi, he feared they might incite each other to rebellion and showed special care in comforting him; Boyu then was at ease.

sentences.zh: 永明元年，與崇祖並見誣伏誅，而胤叔為太子左率。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongming, he and Chongzu were both slandered and executed; Yinshu became Left Commander of the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongming, he and Chongzu were both slandered and executed; Yinshu became Left Commander of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 呂文顯歎曰：「伯玉能謀太祖而不能自謀，豈非天哉。」

translations.literal: Lü Wenxian sighed and said: "Boyu could plot for the Founding Emperor but could not plot for himself—is this not Heaven's will?"
translations.idiomatic: Lü Wenxian sighed and said, "Boyu could plot for the founding emperor but could not plot for himself—is this not Heaven's will?"

sentences.zh: 初，伯玉微時，有善相墓者謂其父曰：「君墓當出暴貴者，但不得久耳；

translations.literal: Initially, when Boyu was still obscure, a skilled grave diviner said to his father: "Your tomb will produce one who rises suddenly to great honor, but he will not last long;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Boyu was still obscure, a skilled grave diviner told his father, "Your tomb will produce one who rises suddenly to great honor, but he will not last long;

sentences.zh: 又出失行女子。」

translations.literal: it will also produce a woman of misconduct."
translations.idiomatic: it will also produce a woman of misconduct.

sentences.zh: 伯玉聞之曰：「朝聞道，夕死可矣。」

translations.literal: When Boyu heard this he said: "If one hears the Way in the morning, one may die in the evening."
translations.idiomatic: When Boyu heard this he said, "If one hears the Way in the morning, one may die in the evening."

sentences.zh: 頃之，伯玉姊當嫁，明日應行，今夕逃隨人去，家尋求不能得。

translations.literal: Before long, Boyu's elder sister was to marry; the wedding was set for the next day, but this night she fled and followed a man away; the family searched but could not find her.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Boyu's elder sister was to marry; the wedding was set for the next day, but that night she fled and followed a man away; the family searched but could not find her.

sentences.zh: 後遂出家為尼。

translations.literal: Later she left home and became a nun.
translations.idiomatic: Later she left home and became a nun.

sentences.zh: 伯玉卒敗亡。

translations.literal: Boyu in the end met defeat and perished.
translations.idiomatic: Boyu in the end met defeat and perished.

sentences.zh: 崔祖思

translations.literal: Cui Zusi
translations.idiomatic: Cui Zusi

sentences.zh: 崔祖思字敬元，清河東武城人，魏中尉琰七世孫也。

translations.literal: Cui Zusi, style name Jingyuan, was a man of Dongwucheng in Qinghe, seventh-generation descendant of Wei Commandant of the Guards Cui Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Zusi, style name Jingyuan, was from Dongwucheng in Qinghe, seventh-generation descendant of Wei Commandant of the Guards Cui Yan.

sentences.zh: 祖諲，宋冀州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shen was Song Inspector of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shen was Song Inspector of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 父僧護，州秀才。

translations.literal: His father Senghu was a provincial xiucai.
translations.idiomatic: His father Senghu was a provincial xiucai.

sentences.zh: 祖思少有志氣，好讀書。

translations.literal: Zusi from youth had lofty spirit and loved reading.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Zusi had lofty spirit and loved reading.

sentences.zh: 年十八，為都昌令，隨青州刺史垣護之入堯廟，廟有蘇侯神偶坐。

translations.literal: At eighteen he was Magistrate of Duchang; he followed the Qingzhou Inspector Yuan Huzhi into the Yao Temple, where the Su Marquis spirit sat as an equal.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he was Magistrate of Duchang. He followed Qingzhou Inspector Yuan Huzhi into the Yao Temple, where the Su Marquis spirit sat as an equal.

sentences.zh: 護之曰：「唐堯聖人而與蘇侯神共坐，今欲正之何如？」

translations.literal: Huzhi said: "Tang Yao was a sage yet sits as equal with the Su Marquis spirit—how about correcting this now?"
translations.idiomatic: Huzhi said, "Tang Yao was a sage yet sits as equal with the Su Marquis spirit—how about correcting this now?

sentences.zh: 祖思曰：「使君若清蕩此坐，則是堯廟重去四凶。」

translations.literal: Zusi said: "If my lord clears away this seat, it will be as if the Yao Temple again drove out the Four Evils."
translations.idiomatic: Zusi said, "If my lord clears away this seat, it will be as if the Yao Temple again drove out the Four Evils."

sentences.zh: 由是諸雜神並除。

translations.literal: From this all miscellaneous spirits were removed together.
translations.idiomatic: From this all miscellaneous spirits were removed together.

sentences.zh: 齊高帝在淮陰，祖思聞風自結，為上輔國主簿，甚見親待，參豫謀議。

translations.literal: When the Qi Emperor Gao was at Huaiyin, Zusi heard of his reputation and attached himself, serving as Chief Clerk to the Supporter of the State, and was greatly treated with intimacy, participating in counsel and deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gao of Qi was at Huaiyin, Zusi heard of his reputation and attached himself, serving as Chief Clerk to the Supporter of the State. He was greatly treated with intimacy and participated in counsel and deliberation.

sentences.zh: 宋朝初議封高帝為梁公，祖思啟高帝曰：「讖云'金刀利刃齊刈之'。

translations.literal: In the Song dynasty, when they first discussed enfeoffing the Emperor Gao as Duke of Liang, Zusi memorialized the Emperor Gao saying: "A prophecy says, 'The golden blade's sharp edge—Qi will mow it down.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song court first discussed enfeoffing Emperor Gao as Duke of Liang, Zusi memorialized him, "A prophecy says, 'The golden blade's sharp edge—Qi will mow it down.

sentences.zh: 今宜稱齊，實應天命。」

translations.literal: Now you should take the name Qi—it truly accords with Heaven's mandate."
translations.idiomatic: Now you should take the name Qi—it truly accords with Heaven's mandate.'

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: He followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: He followed this advice.

sentences.zh: 自相國從事中郎遷齊國內史。

translations.literal: From Attendant of the Chancellor he was transferred to Internal Administrator of the Qi State.
translations.idiomatic: From Attendant of the Chancellor he was transferred to Internal Administrator of the Qi State.

sentences.zh: 高帝既為齊王，置酒為樂，羹膾既至，祖思曰：「此味故為南北所推。」

translations.literal: After the Emperor Gao became King of Qi, he set out wine for pleasure; when the broth and minced meat arrived, Zusi said: "This flavor is indeed prized by north and south alike."
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Gao became King of Qi, he set out wine for pleasure. When the broth and minced meat arrived, Zusi said, "This flavor is indeed prized by north and south alike.

sentences.zh: 侍中沈文季曰：「羹膾吳食，非祖思所解。」

translations.literal: The Attendant-in-Ordinary Shen Wenji said: "Broth and minced meat are Wu food—not something Zusi understands."
translations.idiomatic: Attendant-in-Ordinary Shen Wenji said, "Broth and minced meat are Wu food—not something Zusi understands."

sentences.zh: 祖思曰：「炰鱉鱠鯉，似非句吳之詩。」

translations.literal: Zusi said: "Roasted turtle and minced carp—this seems not to be poetry of Gou Wu."
translations.idiomatic: Zusi said, "Roasted turtle and minced carp—this seems not to be poetry of Gou Wu."

sentences.zh: 文季曰：「千里蓴羹，豈關魯、衛。」

translations.literal: Wenji said: "Water-shield broth from a thousand li—what has that to do with Lu and Wei?"
translations.idiomatic: Wenji said, "Water-shield broth from a thousand li—what has that to do with Lu and Wei?"

sentences.zh: 帝甚悅，曰：「蓴羹故應還沈。」

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly pleased and said: "The water-shield broth ought to go back to Shen after all."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased and said, "The water-shield broth ought to go back to Shen after all."

sentences.zh: 帝之輔政，眾議將加九錫，內外皆贊成之，祖思獨曰：「公以仁恕匡社稷，執股肱之義。

translations.literal: When the Emperor was assisting in government, the multitude discussed adding the Nine Bestowals; inside and outside all approved, but Zusi alone said: "Your Grace, with benevolence and forbearance, has set right the altars of soil and grain and upheld the duty of arm and thigh.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was assisting in government, the multitude discussed adding the Nine Bestowals; inside and outside all approved, but Zusi alone said, "Your Grace, with benevolence and forbearance, has set right the altars of soil and grain and upheld the duty of arm and thigh.

sentences.zh: 君子愛人以德，不宜如此。」

translations.literal: The gentleman loves others through virtue—this is not fitting."
translations.idiomatic: The gentleman loves others through virtue—this is not fitting.

sentences.zh: 帝聞而非之，曰：「祖思遠同荀令，豈孤所望也。」

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard this he took offense and said: "Zusi is far from being like Director Xun—is this what I hoped for from him?"
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard this he took offense and said, "Zusi is far from being like Director Xun—is this what I hoped for from him?"

sentences.zh: 由此不復處任職之官，而禮見甚重。

translations.literal: From this he no longer held an active office, yet was received with ceremony of great weight.
translations.idiomatic: From this he no longer held an active office, yet was received with ceremony of great weight.

sentences.zh: 垣崇祖受密旨參訪朝臣，光祿大夫垣閎曰：「身受宋氏厚恩，復蒙明公眷接，進不敢同，退不敢異。」

translations.literal: Yuan Chongzu received a secret edict to inquire of court ministers. The Household Grandee Yuan Hong said: "I have received the Song clan's thick favor and again been shown the Illustrious Duke's gracious regard—in advancing I dare not agree, in retreating I dare not differ."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Chongzu received a secret edict to inquire of court ministers. Household Grandee Yuan Hong said, "I have received the Song clan's thick favor and again been shown the Illustrious Duke's gracious regard—in advancing I dare not agree, in retreating I dare not differ.

sentences.zh: 祖思又曰：「公退讓誠節，故宜受之以禮。」

translations.literal: Zusi again said: "Your Grace's yielding and sincere integrity—therefore you ought to receive it with ceremony."
translations.idiomatic: Zusi again said, "Your Grace's yielding and sincere integrity—therefore you ought to receive it with ceremony."

sentences.zh: 次問冠軍將軍崔文仲，文仲問崇祖曰：「卿意云何？」

translations.literal: Next they asked the Champion General Cui Wenzhong; Wenzhong asked Chongzu: "What is your view?"
translations.idiomatic: Next they asked Champion General Cui Wenzhong. Wenzhong asked Chongzu, "What is your view?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「聖人云'知幾其神'。

translations.literal: He replied: "The sage said, 'To know the subtle is divine.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "The sage said, 'To know the subtle is divine.

sentences.zh: 又云'見幾而作'。」

translations.literal: He also said, 'When one sees the subtle, act.'"
translations.idiomatic: He also said, 'When one sees the subtle, act.'"

sentences.zh: 文仲撫髀曰：「政與吾意同。」

translations.literal: Wenzhong slapped his thigh and said: "This is just my meaning."
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhong slapped his thigh and said, "This is just my meaning."

sentences.zh: 崇祖具說之。

translations.literal: Chongzu reported all this in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzu reported all this in detail.

sentences.zh: 及帝受禪，閎存故爵，文仲、崇祖皆封侯，祖思加官而已。

translations.literal: When the Emperor received the abdication, Hong kept his former rank; Wenzhong and Chongzu were both enfeoffed as marquises; Zusi received only an additional office.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor received the abdication, Hong kept his former rank; Wenzhong and Chongzu were both enfeoffed as marquises; Zusi received only an additional office.

sentences.zh: 除給事中、黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed Supervising Attendant and Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Supervising Attendant and Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 武帝即位，祖思啟陳政事，以為：「自古開物成務，必以教學為先。

translations.literal: When the Emperor Wu took the throne, Zusi memorialized on state affairs, holding that: "From antiquity, to open things and accomplish tasks, teaching and learning must come first.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu took the throne, Zusi memorialized on state affairs, holding that from antiquity, to open things and accomplish tasks, teaching and learning must come first.

sentences.zh: 宜太廟之南，弘修文序，司農以北，廣開武校。」

translations.literal: South of the Grand Ancestral Temple one should broadly establish literary schools; north of the Minister of Agriculture one should widely open military academies."
translations.idiomatic: South of the Grand Ancestral Temple one should broadly establish literary schools; north of the Minister of Agriculture one should widely open military academies.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「劉備取帳鉤銅鑄錢，以充國用；

translations.literal: He also said: "Liu Bei took the bronze of tent hooks to cast coin and fill state use;
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Liu Bei took the bronze of tent hooks to cast coin and fill state use;

sentences.zh: 魏武遣女皁帳，婢十人；

translations.literal: Wei Wu sent his daughter a black tent and ten maidservants;
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao sent his daughter a black tent and ten maidservants;

sentences.zh: 東阿婦以繡衣賜死；

translations.literal: the woman of Dong'e was granted death by embroidered robe;
translations.idiomatic: the woman of Dong'e was granted death by embroidered robe;

sentences.zh: 王景興以折米見誚；

translations.literal: Wang Jingxing was mocked for breaking rice;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jingxing was mocked for breaking rice;

sentences.zh: 宋武節儉過人，張妃房唯碧綃蚊幬、三齊苮席、五盞盤桃花米飯，殷仲文勸令畜伎，答云：'我不解聲。

translations.literal: Song Wu's frugality surpassed others': Consort Zhang's quarters had only green gauze mosquito nets, a Sanqi rush mat, and five-bowl trays of peach-blossom rice; Yin Zhongwen urged him to keep entertainers, and he answered: 'I do not understand music.'
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Song's frugality surpassed others': Consort Zhang's quarters had only green gauze mosquito nets, a Sanqi rush mat, and five-bowl trays of peach-blossom rice; Yin Zhongwen urged him to keep entertainers, and he answered, 'I do not understand music.'

sentences.zh: '仲文曰：'但畜自解。

translations.literal: Zhongwen said: 'Just keep them—they will understand on their own.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen said, 'Just keep them—they will understand on their own.'

sentences.zh: '又答：'畏解故不畜。

translations.literal: He answered again: 'I fear they would understand, so I do not keep them.
translations.idiomatic: He answered again, 'I fear they would understand, so I do not keep them.

sentences.zh: '曆觀帝王，未嘗不以約素興侈麗亡也。

translations.literal: Surveying emperors and kings through the ages, none ever failed to rise through frugality and perish through extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: Surveying emperors and kings through the ages, none ever failed to rise through frugality and perish through extravagance.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下體唐成儉，踵虞為樸，寢殿則素木卑構，膳器則陶瓢充禦。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that Your Majesty embodies the frugality of Tang and Cheng, follows Yu in simplicity: the sleeping hall is built of plain wood in low structure; dining vessels are earthen ladles filling the imperial use.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly consider that Your Majesty embodies the frugality of Tang and Cheng, follows Yu in simplicity: the sleeping hall is built of plain wood in low structure; dining vessels are earthen ladles filling the imperial use.

sentences.zh: 瓊簪玉笏，碎以為塵；

translations.literal: Jade hairpins and jade tablets were smashed to dust;
translations.idiomatic: Jade hairpins and jade tablets were smashed to dust;

sentences.zh: 珍裘繡服，焚之如草。

translations.literal: precious furs and embroidered robes were burned like grass.
translations.idiomatic: precious furs and embroidered robes were burned like grass.

sentences.zh: 宜察朝士有柴車蓬館，高以殊等，馳禽荒色，長違清編，則調風變俗，不俟終日。」

translations.literal: You should examine court gentlemen who have firewood carts and rush-thatched lodges yet are elevated to special rank, who rush after birds and wilderness pleasures and long violate pure regulations—then harmonizing customs and changing habits need not wait a full day."
translations.idiomatic: You should examine court gentlemen who have firewood carts and rush-thatched lodges yet are elevated to special rank, who rush after birds and wilderness pleasures and long violate pure regulations—then harmonizing customs and changing habits need not wait a full day.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「憲律之重，由來尚矣。

translations.literal: He also said: "The weight of statutes and ordinances has been honored from of old.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "The weight of statutes and ordinances has been honored from of old.

sentences.zh: 實宜清置廷尉，茂簡三官。

translations.literal: It is truly fitting to clearly establish the Court of Justice and abundantly select the three officials.
translations.idiomatic: It is truly fitting to clearly establish the Court of Justice and abundantly select the three officials.

sentences.zh: 漢來習律有家，子孫並傳其業。

translations.literal: Since Han times there have been families skilled in law, whose sons and grandsons all transmitted the profession.
translations.idiomatic: Since Han times there have been families skilled in law, whose sons and grandsons all transmitted the profession.

sentences.zh: 今廷尉律生，乃令史門戶，刑之不厝，抑此之由。」

translations.literal: Now the Court of Justice's law students are merely clerks' households—punishment cannot be set right; this is the reason it is suppressed."
translations.idiomatic: Now the Court of Justice's law students are merely clerks' households—punishment cannot be set right; this is the reason it is suppressed.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「案前漢編戶千萬，太樂伶官方八百二十九人，孔光等奏罷不合經法者四百四十一人，正樂定員唯置三百八十八人。

translations.literal: He also said: "According to Former Han, registered households numbered ten million; the Grand Music Office's performer officials were eight hundred twenty-nine; Kong Guang and others memorialized to dismiss four hundred forty-one who did not accord with canonical law, fixing the proper music establishment at only three hundred eighty-eight persons.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "According to Former Han, registered households numbered ten million; the Grand Music Office's performer officials were eight hundred twenty-nine; Kong Guang and others memorialized to dismiss four hundred forty-one who did not accord with canonical law, fixing the proper music establishment at only three hundred eighty-eight persons.

sentences.zh: 今戶口不能百萬，而太樂雅鄭，元徽時校試千有餘人，後堂雜伎不在其數。

translations.literal: Now households cannot reach one million, yet the Grand Music Office's refined and Zheng music—in the Yuanhui era examination tested more than a thousand, and rear-hall miscellaneous performers are not counted among them.
translations.idiomatic: Now households cannot reach one million, yet the Grand Music Office's refined and Zheng music—in the Yuanhui era examination tested more than a thousand, and rear-hall miscellaneous performers are not counted among them.

sentences.zh: 糜費力役，傷敗風俗。

translations.literal: They waste resources and labor service and injure and ruin customs.
translations.idiomatic: They waste resources and labor service and injure and ruin customs.

sentences.zh: 今欲撥邪歸道，莫若罷雜伎，王庭唯置鍾篽羽戚登歌而已。」

translations.literal: If you now wish to turn away from evil and return to the Way, nothing is better than abolishing miscellaneous performers; the royal court should place only bells, bamboo pipes, feather dancers, and ascending singers."
translations.idiomatic: If you now wish to turn away from evil and return to the Way, nothing is better than abolishing miscellaneous performers; the royal court should place only bells, bamboo pipes, feather dancers, and ascending singers.

sentences.zh: 上詔報答。

translations.literal: The sovereign issued an edict in reply.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign issued an edict in reply.

sentences.zh: 後為青、冀二州刺史，在政清勤，而謙卑下士，言議未嘗及時事，上更以敬重之。

translations.literal: Later he was Qing and Ji Provinces Inspector; in government he was pure and diligent, yet humble and deferential to gentlemen; in speech and discussion he never touched current affairs—the sovereign esteemed him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was Qing and Ji Provinces Inspector; in government he was pure and diligent, yet humble and deferential to gentlemen; in speech and discussion he never touched current affairs—the sovereign esteemed him all the more.

sentences.zh: 未幾卒，上深加嘆惜。

translations.literal: Before long he died; the sovereign deeply sighed in regret.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died; the sovereign deeply sighed in regret.

sentences.zh: 祖思叔父景真，位平昌太守，有惠政，常懸一蒲鞭而未嘗用。

translations.literal: Zusi's uncle by father's side, Jingzhen, held the post of Pingchang Prefect; he had benevolent government and always hung a rush whip but never used it.
translations.idiomatic: Zusi's uncle by father's side, Jingzhen, held the post of Pingchang Prefect; he had benevolent government and always hung a rush whip but never used it.

sentences.zh: 去任之日，土人思之為立祠。

translations.literal: On the day he left his post, the local people, missing him, erected a shrine.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he left his post, the local people, missing him, erected a shrine.

sentences.zh: 子元祖有學行，好屬文，仕至射聲校尉。

translations.literal: His son Yuanzu had learning and conduct, loved composing literary works, and served up to Colonel of the Archers Who Shoot at Sound.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuanzu had learning and conduct, loved composing literary works, and served up to Colonel of the Archers Who Shoot at Sound.

sentences.zh: 武帝取為延昌主帥。

translations.literal: The Emperor Wu took him as Chief of Yan Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu took him as Chief of Yan Chang.

sentences.zh: 從駕至何美人墓，上為悼亡詩，特詔元祖使和，稱以為善。

translations.literal: Accompanying the imperial procession to the tomb of the Beautiful Lady He, the sovereign composed an elegy for the dead; he specially ordered Yuanzu to compose a matching piece and praised it as good.
translations.idiomatic: Accompanying the imperial procession to the tomb of the Beautiful Lady He, the sovereign composed an elegy for the dead; he specially ordered Yuanzu to compose a matching piece and praised it as good.

sentences.zh: 永明九年，魏使李道固及蔣少遊至。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Yongming, Wei envoys Li Daogu and Jiang Shaoyou arrived.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Yongming, Wei envoys Li Daogu and Jiang Shaoyou arrived.

sentences.zh: 元祖言臣甥少游有班、倕之功，今來必令模寫宮掖，未可令反。

translations.literal: Yuanzu said: "My nephew Shaoyou has the achievements of Ban and Dai; if he comes now he will surely be made to copy the palace quarters—it is not permissible to let him return."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzu said, "My nephew Shaoyou has the achievements of Ban and Dai; if he comes now he will surely be made to copy the palace quarters—it is not permissible to let him return."

sentences.zh: 上不從。

translations.literal: The sovereign did not follow this.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign did not follow this.

sentences.zh: 少遊果圖畫而歸。

translations.literal: Shaoyou indeed drew plans and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyou indeed drew plans and returned.

sentences.zh: 元祖歷位驍騎將軍，出為東海太守。

translations.literal: Yuanzu successively held the post of Valiant Cavalry General and went out as Donghai Prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzu successively held the post of Valiant Cavalry General and went out as Donghai Prefect.

sentences.zh: 上每思之，時節恒賜手敕，賞賜有加。

translations.literal: The sovereign often thought of him; at seasons and festivals he always bestowed handwritten edicts, with rewards and gifts added.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign often thought of him; at seasons and festivals he always bestowed handwritten edicts, with rewards and gifts added.

sentences.zh: 時青州刺史張沖啟：「淮北頻歲不熟，今秋始稔。

translations.literal: At that time Qingzhou Inspector Zhang Chong memorialized: "North of the Huai has for years not ripened; this autumn it has first ripened.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Qingzhou Inspector Zhang Chong memorialized, "North of the Huai has for years not ripened; this autumn it has first ripened.

sentences.zh: 此境鄰接戎寇，彌須沃實，乞權斷穀過淮南。」

translations.literal: This region borders on barbarian raiders and all the more needs rich sufficiency; I beg permission to cut off grain passing south of the Huai."
translations.idiomatic: This region borders on barbarian raiders and all the more needs rich sufficiency; I beg permission to cut off grain passing south of the Huai.

sentences.zh: 而徐、兗、豫、司諸州又各私斷谷米，不聽出境，自是江北荒儉，有流亡之弊。

translations.literal: But Xu, Yan, Yu, and Si provinces each on their own cut off grain and rice and would not permit it to leave their borders; from this the north of the river was barren and lean, with the harm of displaced refugees.
translations.idiomatic: But Xu, Yan, Yu, and Si provinces each on their own cut off grain and rice and would not permit it to leave their borders; from this the north of the river was barren and lean, with the harm of displaced refugees.

sentences.zh: 元祖乃上書，謂宜豐儉均之。

translations.literal: Yuanzu thereupon submitted a memorial, saying abundance and scarcity should be equalized.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzu thereupon submitted a memorial, saying abundance and scarcity should be equalized.

sentences.zh: 書奏見從。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted it was followed.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted it was followed.

sentences.zh: 祖思宗人文仲，位徐州刺史，封建陽縣子，在政為百姓所懼。

translations.literal: Zusi's clansman Wenzhong held the post of Xuzhou Inspector, was enfeoffed as Viscount of Jianyang, and in government was feared by the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Zusi's clansman Wenzhong held the post of Xuzhou Inspector, was enfeoffed as Viscount of Jianyang, and in government was feared by the common people.

sentences.zh: 除黃門侍郎，領越騎校尉，徙封隨縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, concurrently Colonel of the Exotic Cavalry, and transferred enfeoffment to Sui County.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, concurrently Colonel of the Exotic Cavalry, and transferred enfeoffment to Sui County.

sentences.zh: 嘗獻高帝纏須繩一枚，上納受。

translations.literal: He once presented the Emperor Gao one rope for binding the beard; the sovereign accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: He once presented Emperor Gao one rope for binding the beard; the sovereign accepted it.

sentences.zh: 後卒于汝陰太守，贈徐州刺史，諡襄子。

translations.literal: Later he died as Ruyin Prefect; posthumously he was given Xuzhou Inspector and the posthumous title Viscount Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Later he died as Ruyin Prefect; posthumously he was given Xuzhou Inspector and the posthumous title Viscount Xiang.

sentences.zh: 蘇侃字休烈，武邑人也。

translations.literal: Su Kan, style name Xiulie, was a man of Wuyi.
translations.idiomatic: Su Kan, style name Xiulie, was from Wuyi.

sentences.zh: 祖護，本郡太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Hu was Prefect of the native commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Hu was Prefect of the native commandery.

sentences.zh: 父端，州中從事。

translations.literal: His father Duan was a provincial attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His father Duan was a provincial attendant.

sentences.zh: 侃涉獵書傳，薛安都反，引侃為其府參軍，使掌書記。

translations.literal: Kan ranged widely through books and records. When Xue Andu rebelled, he drew Kan as staff officer in his headquarters and had him oversee documents.
translations.idiomatic: Kan ranged widely through books and records. When Xue Andu rebelled, he drew Kan as staff officer in his headquarters and had him oversee documents.

sentences.zh: 侃自拔南歸，齊高帝在淮上，便自委結。

translations.literal: Kan extricated himself and returned south; the Qi Emperor Gao was on the Huai and he at once attached himself.
translations.idiomatic: Kan extricated himself and returned south; Emperor Gao of Qi was on the Huai and he at once attached himself.

sentences.zh: 高帝鎮淮陰，取為冠軍錄事參軍。

translations.literal: When the Emperor Gao garrisoned Huaiyin, he took him as Champion General's Records Staff Officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gao garrisoned Huaiyin, he took him as Champion General's Records Staff Officer.

sentences.zh: 時高帝在兵久見疑，乃作塞客吟以喻志曰：

translations.literal: At that time the Emperor Gao, long in command of troops, was under suspicion; he therefore composed the "Frontier Traveler's Chant" to express his intent, saying:
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Gao, long in command of troops, was under suspicion; he therefore composed the "Frontier Traveler's Chant" to express his intent, saying:

sentences.zh: 寶緯紊宗，神經淡序，德晦河、晉，曆宣江、楚。

translations.literal: The precious warp tangled the lineage; the spirit warp thinned the order; virtue was hidden in He and Jin, the calendar proclaimed in Jiang and Chu.
translations.idiomatic: The precious warp tangled the lineage; the spirit warp thinned the order; virtue was hidden in He and Jin, the calendar proclaimed in Jiang and Chu.

sentences.zh: 雲雷兆壯，天山繇武。

translations.literal: Cloud and thunder foretold vigor; Heaven Mountain summoned arms.
translations.idiomatic: Cloud and thunder foretold vigor; Heaven Mountain summoned arms.

sentences.zh: 直髮指秦關，凝精越漢渚。

translations.literal: With hair unbound I point to Qin Pass; gathering spirit I cross Han's ford.
translations.idiomatic: With hair unbound I point to Qin Pass; gathering spirit I cross Han's ford.

sentences.zh: 秋風起，塞草衰，鵰鴻思，邊馬悲。

translations.literal: Autumn wind rises; frontier grass withers; the eagle-goose longs; border horses grieve.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn wind rises; frontier grass withers; the eagle-goose longs; border horses grieve.

sentences.zh: 平原千里顧，但見轉蓬飛。

translations.literal: Over the thousand-li plain I look back—only tumbling tumbleweed flying.
translations.idiomatic: Over the thousand-li plain I look back—only tumbling tumbleweed flying.

sentences.zh: 星嚴海淨，月澈河明，清暉映幕，素液凝庭。

translations.literal: Stars stern, sea clear; moon limpid, river bright; clear radiance shines on the tent; white dew congeals in the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: Stars stern, sea clear; moon limpid, river bright; clear radiance shines on the tent; white dew congeals in the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 金笳夜厲，羽轊晨征。

translations.literal: Golden reed-pipes keen by night; feathered wheels march at dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Golden reed-pipes keen by night; feathered wheels march at dawn.

sentences.zh: 斡晴潭而悵泗，枻松洲而悼情。

translations.literal: Turning the clear pool I grieve for Si; plying oars at Pine Islet I mourn in feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Turning the clear pool I grieve for Si; plying oars at Pine Islet I mourn in feeling.

sentences.zh: 蘭涵風而寫豔，菊籠泉而散英。

translations.literal: Orchid holds wind and writes its splendor; chrysanthemum cages spring and scatters its blooms.
translations.idiomatic: Orchid holds wind and writes its splendor; chrysanthemum cages spring and scatters its blooms.

sentences.zh: 曲繞首燕之歎，吹軫絕越之聲。

translations.literal: The tune winds with the swallow's lament at its head; the pipe sounds the music that transcends Yue.
translations.idiomatic: The tune winds with the swallow's lament at its head; the pipe sounds the music that transcends Yue.

sentences.zh: 欷園琴之孤弄，想庭藿之餘馨。

translations.literal: Sighing at the garden zither's solitary playing, I think of the courtyard bean's lingering fragrance.
translations.idiomatic: Sighing at the garden zither's solitary playing, I think of the courtyard bean's lingering fragrance.

sentences.zh: 青關望斷，白日西斜，恬源靚霧，壟首暉霞。

translations.literal: Green Pass—gazing breaks off; white sun slants west; tranquil spring shows fair mist; mound crest glows with dawn clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Green Pass—gazing breaks off; white sun slants west; tranquil spring shows fair mist; mound crest glows with dawn clouds.

sentences.zh: 戒旋鷁，躍還波。

translations.literal: Warning the turning petrel, leaping back on returning waves.
translations.idiomatic: Warning the turning petrel, leaping back on returning waves.

sentences.zh: 情綿綿而方遠，思褭褭而遂多。

translations.literal: Feeling stretches on and just grows distant; thought trails thin and grows ever more.
translations.idiomatic: Feeling stretches on and just grows distant; thought trails thin and grows ever more.

sentences.zh: 粵擊秦中之築，因為塞上之歌。

translations.literal: Thus striking the Qin-land drumbeat, I thereby make a frontier song.
translations.idiomatic: Thus striking the Qin-land drumbeat, I thereby make a frontier song.

sentences.zh: 歌曰：朝發兮江泉，日夕兮陵山。

translations.literal: The song says: At dawn I set out from river springs; at dusk I reach hill ranges.
translations.idiomatic: The song says: At dawn I set out from river springs; at dusk I reach hill ranges.

sentences.zh: 驚飆兮瀄汨，淮流兮潺湲。

translations.literal: Startling gale—rushing torrent; Huai current—murmuring flow.
translations.idiomatic: Startling gale—rushing torrent; Huai current—murmuring flow.

sentences.zh: 胡埃兮雲聚，楚旆兮星懸。

translations.literal: Barbarian dust—clouds gather; Chu banners—stars hang.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarian dust—clouds gather; Chu banners—stars hang.

sentences.zh: 愁墉兮思宇，惻愴兮何言。

translations.literal: Sorrow walls—thought of home; anguished—what words?
translations.idiomatic: Sorrow walls—thought of home; anguished—what words?

sentences.zh: 定寰中之逸鑒，審雕陵之迷泉。

translations.literal: Fix the far mirror within the realm; examine the lost spring at Diao Mound.
translations.idiomatic: Fix the far mirror within the realm; examine the lost spring at Diao Mound.

sentences.zh: 悟樊籠之或累，悵遐心以棲玄。

translations.literal: Awaken that the cage may bind; grieve that the far heart would dwell in mystery.
translations.idiomatic: Awaken that the cage may bind; grieve that the far heart would dwell in mystery.

sentences.zh: 侃達高帝此旨，更自勤厲，遂見委以府事，深被知待。

translations.literal: Kan grasped the Emperor Gao's intent in this and redoubled his own diligence; he was then entrusted with headquarters affairs and deeply known and favored.
translations.idiomatic: Kan grasped Emperor Gao's intent in this and redoubled his own diligence; he was then entrusted with headquarters affairs and deeply known and favored.

sentences.zh: 桂陽之難，帝以侃為平南錄事，領軍主，從頓新亭，使分金銀賦賜將士。

translations.literal: In the Guiyang crisis the Emperor made Kan Pacify-the-South Records Officer, commanding army masters; he followed in encamping at Xinting and was ordered to distribute gold and silver rewards and gifts to officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In the Guiyang crisis the emperor made Kan Pacify-the-South Records Officer, commanding army masters; he followed in encamping at Xinting and was ordered to distribute gold and silver rewards and gifts to officers and soldiers.

sentences.zh: 後為帝太尉諮議。

translations.literal: Later he was the Emperor's Grand Commandant Adviser.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was the emperor's Grand Commandant Adviser.

sentences.zh: 侃事高帝既久，備悉起居，乃與丘巨源撰蕭太尉記，載帝征伐之功。

translations.literal: Kan had served the Emperor Gao long and knew his daily conduct fully; he then with Qiu Juyuan compiled the Record of the Grand Commandant Xiao, recording the Emperor's campaigns and achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Kan had served Emperor Gao long and knew his daily conduct fully; he then with Qiu Juyuan compiled the Record of the Grand Commandant Xiao, recording the emperor's campaigns and achievements.

sentences.zh: 封新建縣侯。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xinjian County.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xinjian County.

sentences.zh: 虞悰字景豫，會稽余姚人也。

translations.literal: Yu Cong, style name Jingyu, was a man of Yuyao in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Cong, style name Jingyu, was from Yuyao in Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 祖嘯父，晉左戶尚書。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xiaofu was Jin Left Household Minister.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xiaofu was Jin Left Household Minister.

sentences.zh: 父秀之，黃門郎。

translations.literal: His father Xiuzhi was Huangmen Lang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xiuzhi was Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 悰少以孝聞，父病不欲見人，雖子弟亦不得前，時悰年十二三，晝夜伏戶外問內豎消息。

translations.literal: Cong from youth was known for filial piety; when his father was ill he would not see people—even sons and younger brothers could not approach. At that time Cong was twelve or thirteen; day and night he lay prostrate outside the door asking the inner attendants for news.
translations.idiomatic: Cong from youth was known for filial piety; when his father was ill he would not see people—even sons and younger brothers could not approach. At that time Cong was twelve or thirteen; day and night he lay prostrate outside the door asking the inner attendants for news.

sentences.zh: 問未知，轉嗚咽流涕，如此者百餘日。

translations.literal: When he asked and did not yet know, he would turn to sobbing and shedding tears—thus for more than a hundred days.
translations.idiomatic: When he asked and did not yet know, he would turn to sobbing and shedding tears—thus for more than a hundred days.

sentences.zh: 及亡，終喪日唯食麥鉡二枚。

translations.literal: When his father died, throughout the mourning period each day he ate only two wheat cakes.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died, throughout the mourning period each day he ate only two wheat cakes.

sentences.zh: 仕宋位黃門郎。

translations.literal: Serving Song, he held the post of Huangmen Lang.
translations.idiomatic: Serving Song, he held the post of Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 宋明帝誅山陽王休佑，至葬日，寒雪厚三尺，故人無至者，唯悰一人來赴。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming of Song executed the Prince of Shanyang, Xiuyou; on the burial day cold snow lay three feet deep and none of his old friends came—only Cong alone came to attend.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming of Song executed the Prince of Shanyang, Xiuyou; on the burial day cold snow lay three feet deep and none of his old friends came—only Cong alone came to attend.

sentences.zh: 初，齊武帝始從宦，家尚貧薄，悰數相分遺。

translations.literal: Initially, when the Qi Emperor Wu first entered official service, his family was still poor and thin; Cong repeatedly shared gifts with him.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, when the future Emperor Wu of Qi first entered official service, his family was still poor and thin; Cong repeatedly shared gifts with him.

sentences.zh: 每行必呼帝同載，帝甚德之。

translations.literal: Whenever he traveled he always called the Emperor to ride together; the Emperor was deeply grateful.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he traveled he always called the emperor to ride together; the emperor was deeply grateful.

sentences.zh: 齊建元初，為太子中庶子，累遷豫章內史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qi Jianyuan he was Crown Prince Central Attendant and was repeatedly transferred to Yuzhang Internal Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Qi Jianyuan he was Crown Prince Central Attendant and was repeatedly transferred to Yuzhang Internal Administrator.

sentences.zh: 悰家富於財而善為滋味，豫章王嶷盛饌享賓，謂悰曰：「肴羞有所遺不？」

translations.literal: Cong's family was rich in wealth and skilled in flavors; the Prince of Yuzhang, Ye, set out a lavish feast for guests and said to Cong: "Are there any delicacies you have left over?"
translations.idiomatic: Cong's family was rich in wealth and skilled in flavors; Prince Ye of Yuzhang set out a lavish feast for guests and said to Cong, "Are there any delicacies you have left over?

sentences.zh: 悰曰：「何曾食疏有黃頷臛，恨無之。」

translations.literal: Cong said: "In He Zeng's food notes there is yellow-jaw broth—I regret not having it."
translations.idiomatic: Cong said, "In He Zeng's food notes there is yellow-jaw broth—I regret not having it."

sentences.zh: 累遷太子右率。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly transferred to Crown Prince Right Commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly transferred to Crown Prince Right Commander.

sentences.zh: 永明八年大水，百官戎服救太廟，悰朱衣乘車鹵簿，于宣陽門外入行馬內驅逐人，被奏見原。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yongming there was great flooding; the hundred officials in military dress rescued the Grand Ancestral Temple. Cong, in red robes riding a carriage with imperial guards, inside the traveling-horse zone at Xuanyang Gate drove people away; he was memorialized against but pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Yongming there was great flooding; the hundred officials in military dress rescued the Grand Ancestral Temple. Cong, in red robes riding a carriage with imperial guards, inside the traveling-horse zone at Xuanyang Gate drove people away; he was memorialized against but pardoned.

sentences.zh: 上以悰布衣之舊，從容謂悰曰：「我當令卿復祖業。」

translations.literal: The sovereign, because of Cong's old ties as a commoner, said at ease to Cong: "I shall have you restore your family's profession."
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign, because of Cong's old ties as a commoner, said at ease to Cong, "I shall have you restore your family's profession.

sentences.zh: 轉侍中，朝廷咸驚其美。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attendant-in-Ordinary; the court all marveled at his excellence.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Attendant-in-Ordinary; the court all marveled at his excellence.

sentences.zh: 遷祠部尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 武帝幸芳林園就悰求味，悰獻粣及雜肴數十輿，太官鼎味不及也。

translations.literal: The Emperor Wu visited the Fragrant Grove Garden and asked Cong for flavors; Cong presented coarse grain and miscellaneous dishes in several dozen carts—the Imperial Kitchen's cauldron flavors could not match them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu visited the Fragrant Grove Garden and asked Cong for flavors; Cong presented coarse grain and miscellaneous dishes in several dozen carts—the Imperial Kitchen's cauldron flavors could not match them.

sentences.zh: 上就悰求諸飲食方，悰秘不出。

translations.literal: The sovereign asked Cong for all his food and drink recipes; Cong kept them secret and would not produce them.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign asked Cong for all his food and drink recipes; Cong kept them secret and would not produce them.

sentences.zh: 上醉後體不快，悰乃獻醒酒鯖鮓一方而已。

translations.literal: When the sovereign after drunkenness felt unwell in body, Cong then presented only one recipe for sobering mackerel pickle.
translations.idiomatic: When the sovereign after drunkenness felt unwell in body, Cong then presented only one recipe for sobering mackerel pickle.

sentences.zh: 郁林王立，兼大匠卿，起休安陵，於陵所受局下牛酒，坐免官。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yulin was established, Cong concurrently held the post of Grand Master of Works and raised the Xiuan Mausoleum; for oxen and wine received from subordinates at the mausoleum he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yulin was established, Cong concurrently held the post of Grand Master of Works and raised the Xiuan Mausoleum; for oxen and wine received from subordinates at the mausoleum he was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 隆昌元年，以白衣領職。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longchang he held the post in plain dress.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Longchang he held the post in plain dress.

sentences.zh: 郁林廢，悰竊歎曰：「王、徐遂縛袴廢天子，天下豈有此理耶？」

translations.literal: When Yulin was deposed, Cong sighed privately: "Wang and Xu have bound their trousers and deposed the Son of Heaven—can there be such a principle under Heaven?"
translations.idiomatic: When Yulin was deposed, Cong sighed privately, "Wang and Xu have bound their trousers and deposed the Son of Heaven—can there be such a principle under Heaven?

sentences.zh: 延興元年，領右軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yanxing he led the Right Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yanxing he led the Right Army.

sentences.zh: 明帝立，悰稱疾不陪位。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming was established, Cong claimed illness and did not take part in the enthronement.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming was established, Cong claimed illness and did not take part in the enthronement.

sentences.zh: 帝使尚書令王晏齎廢立事示悰，以悰舊人，引參佐命。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent Secretariat Director Wang Yan to carry the matter of deposition and establishment to show Cong; because Cong was an old associate, he was invited to participate in assisting the mandate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Secretariat Director Wang Yan to carry the matter of deposition and establishment to show Cong; because Cong was an old associate, he was invited to participate in assisting the mandate.

sentences.zh: 悰謂晏曰：「主上聖明，公卿戮力，寧假朽老以匡贊惟新乎，不敢聞命。」

translations.literal: Cong said to Yan: "The sovereign is sagely and bright; the dukes and ministers exert their strength together—would you borrow a decayed old man to assist the renewal? I dare not accept the command."
translations.idiomatic: Cong said to Yan, "The sovereign is sagely and bright; the dukes and ministers exert their strength together—would you borrow a decayed old man to assist the renewal? I dare not accept the command.

sentences.zh: 因慟不自勝。

translations.literal: He thereupon grieved beyond controlling himself.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon grieved beyond controlling himself.

sentences.zh: 朝議欲糾之，僕射徐孝嗣曰：「此亦古之遺直。」

translations.literal: Court discussion wished to censure him; Vice Director Xu Xiaosi said: "This too is an upright remnant of antiquity."
translations.idiomatic: Court discussion wished to censure him; Vice Director Xu Xiaosi said, "This too is an upright remnant of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 眾議乃止。

translations.literal: The multitude's discussion then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The multitude's discussion then ceased.

sentences.zh: 悰稱疾篤還東，詔賜假百日。

translations.literal: Cong claimed serious illness and returned east; an edict granted him leave for a hundred days.
translations.idiomatic: Cong claimed serious illness and returned east; an edict granted him leave for a hundred days.

sentences.zh: 轉給事中、光祿大夫，尋加正員常侍，卒。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Supervising Attendant and Household Grandee; soon added regular Attendant-in-Ordinary; he died.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Supervising Attendant and Household Grandee; soon added regular Attendant-in-Ordinary; he died.

sentences.zh: 悰性敦實，與人知識，必相存訪，親疏皆有終始，世以此稱之。

translations.literal: Cong's nature was solid and sincere; with people he knew he always visited and inquired after them; whether close or distant all had proper beginning and end; the age praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Cong's nature was solid and sincere; with people he knew he always visited and inquired after them; whether close or distant all had proper beginning and end; the age praised him for this.

sentences.zh: 胡諧之

translations.literal: Hu Xiezhi
translations.idiomatic: Hu Xiezhi

sentences.zh: 胡諧之，豫章南昌人也。

translations.literal: Hu Xiezhi was a man of Nanchang in Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Xiezhi was from Nanchang in Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 祖廉之，書侍御史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Lianzhi was Attendant Censor for Documents.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Lianzhi was Attendant Censor for Documents.

sentences.zh: 父翼之，州辟不就。

translations.literal: His father Yizhi was summoned by the province but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yizhi was summoned by the province but did not accept.

sentences.zh: 諧之仕宋為邵陵王左軍諮議。

translations.literal: Xiezhi served Song as Staff Adviser to the Left Army of the Prince of Shaoling.
translations.idiomatic: Xiezhi served Song as Staff Adviser to the Left Army of the Prince of Shaoling.

sentences.zh: 齊武帝為江州，以諧之為別駕，委以事任。

translations.literal: When the Qi Emperor Wu was Jiangzhou Inspector, he took Xiezhi as Vice Director and entrusted him with affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the future Emperor Wu of Qi was Jiangzhou Inspector, he took Xiezhi as Vice Director and entrusted him with affairs.

sentences.zh: 建元二年，為給事中、驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianyuan he was Supervising Attendant and Valiant Cavalry General.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianyuan he was Supervising Attendant and Valiant Cavalry General.

sentences.zh: 上方欲獎以貴族盛姻，以諧之家人語傒音不正，乃遣宮內四五人往諧之家教子女語。

translations.literal: The sovereign wished to reward him with a noble marriage alliance; because Xiezhi's family spoke with incorrect Xi pronunciation, he sent four or five people from within the palace to Xiezhi's home to teach the children speech.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign wished to reward him with a noble marriage alliance; because Xiezhi's family spoke with incorrect Xi pronunciation, he sent four or five people from within the palace to Xiezhi's home to teach the children speech.

sentences.zh: 二年後，帝問曰：「卿家人語音已正未？」

translations.literal: Two years later the Emperor asked: "Has your family's speech been corrected yet?"
translations.idiomatic: Two years later the emperor asked, "Has your family's speech been corrected yet?

sentences.zh: 諧之答曰：「宮人少，臣家人多，非唯不能得正音，遂使宮人頓成傒語。」

translations.literal: Xiezhi replied: "There are few people in the palace; my family has many—not only could they not get correct pronunciation, they even made the palace people turn into Xi speakers."
translations.idiomatic: Xiezhi replied, "There are few people in the palace; my family has many—not only could they not get correct pronunciation, they even made the palace people turn into Xi speakers."

sentences.zh: 帝大笑，遍向朝臣說之。

translations.literal: The Emperor laughed greatly and told all the court gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed greatly and told all the court gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 永明五年，為左衛將軍，加給事中。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yongming he was Left Guard General, with added Supervising Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Yongming he was Left Guard General, with added Supervising Attendant.

sentences.zh: 諧之風采瑰潤，善自居處，兼以舊恩見遇，朝士多與交遊。

translations.literal: Xiezhi's bearing was splendid and lustrous; he knew how to comport himself well; together with old favor he was met with; many court gentlemen associated with him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiezhi's bearing was splendid and lustrous; he knew how to comport himself well; together with old favor he was met with; many court gentlemen associated with him.

sentences.zh: 六年，遷都官尚書。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to Minister of the Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was transferred to Minister of the Capital.

sentences.zh: 上欲遷諧之，嘗從容謂曰：「江州有幾侍中邪？」

translations.literal: The sovereign wished to transfer Xiezhi and once said at ease: "How many Attendants-in-Ordinary does Jiangzhou have?"
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign wished to transfer Xiezhi and once said at ease, "How many Attendants-in-Ordinary does Jiangzhou have?

sentences.zh: 答曰：「近世唯程道惠一人而已。」

translations.literal: He replied: "In recent times only Cheng Daohui alone."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "In recent times only Cheng Daohui alone."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「當令有二。」

translations.literal: The sovereign said: "I shall make it two."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I shall make it two."

sentences.zh: 後以語尚書令王儉，儉意更異，乃以為太子中庶子，領左衛率。

translations.literal: Later he told this to Secretariat Director Wang Jian; Jian's intent differed further, and so he was made Crown Prince Central Attendant, leading Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Later he told this to Secretariat Director Wang Jian; Jian's intent differed further, and so he was made Crown Prince Central Attendant, leading Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 諧之有識具，每朝廷官缺及應遷代，密量上所用人，皆如其言。

translations.literal: Xiezhi had insight and capacity; whenever court offices were vacant and should be filled or transferred, he secretly gauged whom the sovereign would use—all matched his words.
translations.idiomatic: Xiezhi had insight and capacity; whenever court offices were vacant and should be filled or transferred, he secretly gauged whom the sovereign would use—all matched his words.

sentences.zh: 虞悰以此稱服之。

translations.literal: Yu Cong for this praised and admired him.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Cong for this praised and admired him.

sentences.zh: 既居權要，多所徵求。

translations.literal: Once he held weighty power, he made many demands.
translations.idiomatic: Once he held weighty power, he made many demands.

sentences.zh: 就梁州刺史范柏年求佳馬，柏年患之，謂使曰：「馬非狗子，那可得為應無極之求。」

translations.literal: He asked Liangzhou Inspector Fan Bonian for fine horses; Bonian resented this and said to the envoy: "Horses are not puppies—how can one answer boundless demands?"
translations.idiomatic: He asked Liangzhou Inspector Fan Bonian for fine horses; Bonian resented this and said to the envoy, "Horses are not puppies—how can one answer boundless demands?

sentences.zh: 接使人薄，使人致恨歸，謂諧之曰：「柏年云，胡諧是何傒狗，無厭之求。」

translations.literal: The envoy was treated poorly; the envoy bore resentment on returning and said to Xiezhi: "Bonian said, What Xi dog is Hu Xie—demands without end."
translations.idiomatic: The envoy was treated poorly; the envoy bore resentment on returning and said to Xiezhi, "Bonian said, What Xi dog is Hu Xie—demands without end."

sentences.zh: 諧之切齒致忿。

translations.literal: Xiezhi ground his teeth in rage.
translations.idiomatic: Xiezhi ground his teeth in rage.

sentences.zh: 時王玄邈代柏年，柏年稱疾推遷不時還。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Xuanyao replaced Bonian; Bonian claimed illness and delayed transfer, not returning in time.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wang Xuanyao replaced Bonian; Bonian claimed illness and delayed transfer, not returning in time.

sentences.zh: 諧之言於帝曰：「柏年恃其山川險固，聚眾欲擅一州。」

translations.literal: Xiezhi spoke to the Emperor: "Bonian relies on his mountains and rivers' perilous strength, gathers crowds and wishes to monopolize a province.
translations.idiomatic: Xiezhi spoke to the emperor, "Bonian relies on his mountains and rivers' perilous strength, gathers crowds and wishes to monopolize a province.

sentences.zh: 及柏年下，帝欲不問，諧之又言：「見獸格得而放上山。」

translations.literal: When Bonian came down the Emperor wished not to question him; Xiezhi again said: "Seeing a beast in the trap and releasing it back up the mountain."
translations.idiomatic: When Bonian came down the emperor wished not to question him; Xiezhi again said, "Seeing a beast in the trap and releasing it back up the mountain."

sentences.zh: 於是賜死。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he was granted death.

sentences.zh: 十年，諧之轉度支尚書，領衛尉。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Xiezhi was transferred to Minister of Revenue, leading Commandant of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Xiezhi was transferred to Minister of Revenue, leading Commandant of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 明年卒，諡肅侯。

translations.literal: The next year he died; posthumous title Marquis Su.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he died; posthumous title Marquis Su.

sentences.zh: 柏年本梓潼人，土斷屬梁州華陽郡。

translations.literal: Bonian was originally from Zitong; through territorial allocation he belonged to Huayang Commandery in Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Bonian was originally from Zitong; through territorial allocation he belonged to Huayang Commandery in Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 初為州將，劉亮使出都諮事，見宋明帝。

translations.literal: Initially he was a provincial officer; Liu Liang sent him to the capital on business and he saw Emperor Ming of Song.
translations.idiomatic: Initially he was a provincial officer; Liu Liang sent him to the capital on business and he saw Emperor Ming of Song.

sentences.zh: 帝言次及廣州貪泉，因問柏年：「卿州復有此水不？」

translations.literal: In conversation the Emperor came to the Greedy Spring of Guangzhou and asked Bonian: "Does your province also have this water?"
translations.idiomatic: In conversation the emperor came to the Greedy Spring of Guangzhou and asked Bonian, "Does your province also have this water?

sentences.zh: 答曰：「梁州唯有文川、武鄉，廉泉、讓水。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Liangzhou has only Literary River and Martial Township, Integrity Spring and Yielding Water."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Liangzhou has only Literary River and Martial Township, Integrity Spring and Yielding Water."

sentences.zh: 又問：「卿宅在何處？」

translations.literal: He again asked: "Where is your residence?"
translations.idiomatic: He again asked, "Where is your residence?

sentences.zh: 曰：「臣所居廉讓之間。」

translations.literal: He said: "Your subject dwells between Integrity and Yielding."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Your subject dwells between Integrity and Yielding."

sentences.zh: 帝嗟其善答，因見知。

translations.literal: The Emperor sighed at his fine reply and thereby came to know him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed at his fine reply and thereby came to know him.

sentences.zh: 歷位內外，終於梁州刺史。

translations.literal: He held posts inside and outside and ended as Liangzhou Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: He held posts inside and outside and ended as Liangzhou Inspector.

sentences.zh: 虞玩之

translations.literal: Yu Wanzhi
translations.idiomatic: Yu Wanzhi

sentences.zh: 虞玩之字茂瑤，會稽余姚人也。

translations.literal: Yu Wanzhi, style name Maoyao, was a man of Yuyao in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Wanzhi, style name Maoyao, was from Yuyao in Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 祖宗，晉尚書庫部郎。

translations.literal: His ancestor Zong was Jin Minister of the Arsenal.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestor Zong was Jin Minister of the Arsenal.

sentences.zh: 父玫，通直常侍。

translations.literal: His father Mei was Direct Transmission Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His father Mei was Direct Transmission Attendant.

sentences.zh: 玩之少閑刀筆，泛涉書史。

translations.literal: Wanzhi from youth was skilled with documents and broadly read histories.
translations.idiomatic: Wanzhi from youth was skilled with documents and broadly read histories.

sentences.zh: 仕宋為烏程令。

translations.literal: Serving Song he was Magistrate of Wucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Serving Song he was Magistrate of Wucheng.

sentences.zh: 路太后外親朱仁彌犯罪，玩之依法案之。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager Lu's maternal relative Zhu Renmi committed a crime; Wanzhi judged the case according to law.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager Lu's maternal relative Zhu Renmi committed a crime; Wanzhi judged the case according to law.

sentences.zh: 太后怨訴孝武，坐免官。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager complained to Emperor Xiaowu; he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager complained to Emperor Xiaowu; he was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 元徽中，為尚書右丞。

translations.literal: In Yuanhui he was Right Assistant Minister of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhui he was Right Assistant Minister of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 齊高帝參政，與玩之書曰：「張華為度支尚書，事不徒然。

translations.literal: When the Qi Emperor Gao assisted in government he wrote to Wanzhi: "Zhang Hua as Minister of Revenue—the affair was not in vain.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gao of Qi assisted in government he wrote to Wanzhi, "Zhang Hua as Minister of Revenue—the affair was not in vain.

sentences.zh: 今漕藏有闕，吾賢居右丞，已覺金粟可積也。」

translations.literal: Now the transport stores have gaps; my worthy man holds the right assistant post—I already feel gold and grain can be accumulated.
translations.idiomatic: Now the transport stores have gaps; my worthy man holds the right assistant post—I already feel gold and grain can be accumulated.

sentences.zh: 玩之上表，陳府庫錢帛，器械役力，所懸轉多，興用漸廣，慮不支歲月。

translations.literal: Wanzhi submitted a memorial stating that the headquarters' cash, silk, implements, labor, and suspended items grew ever more, expenditures gradually widened, and he feared they would not last the year.
translations.idiomatic: Wanzhi submitted a memorial stating that the headquarters' cash, silk, implements, labor, and suspended items grew ever more, expenditures gradually widened, and he feared they would not last the year.

sentences.zh: 朝議優報之。
