translations.literal: Court discussion favorably replied.
translations.idiomatic: Court discussion favorably replied.

sentences.zh: 高帝鎮東府，朝廷致敬，玩之為少府，猶躡屐造席。

translations.literal: When the Emperor Gao garrisoned the Eastern Headquarters, the court showed respect; Wanzhi was Minister of the Privy Purse and still wore clogs to take his seat.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gao garrisoned the Eastern Headquarters, the court showed respect; Wanzhi was Minister of the Privy Purse and still wore clogs to take his seat.

sentences.zh: 高帝取屐親視之，訛黑斜銳，蒵斷以芒接之。

translations.literal: The Emperor Gao took the clog and examined it personally—worn black, slanting and sharp, the rush broken and joined with awn.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao took the clog and examined it personally—worn black, slanting and sharp, the rush broken and joined with awn.

sentences.zh: 問曰：「卿此屐已幾載？」

translations.literal: He asked: "How many years have you worn these clogs?"
translations.idiomatic: He asked, "How many years have you worn these clogs?

sentences.zh: 玩之曰：「初釋褐拜征北行佐買之，著已三十年，貧士竟不辦易。」

translations.literal: Wanzhi said: "When I first left the cloth and was appointed Northern Expedition traveling staff officer I bought them; I have worn them thirty years—a poor gentleman truly cannot afford to replace them."
translations.idiomatic: Wanzhi said, "When I first left the cloth and was appointed Northern Expedition traveling staff officer I bought them; I have worn them thirty years—a poor gentleman truly cannot afford to replace them."

sentences.zh: 高帝咨嗟，因賜以新屐。

translations.literal: The Emperor Gao sighed in admiration and bestowed new clogs.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao sighed in admiration and bestowed new clogs.

sentences.zh: 玩之不受。

translations.literal: Wanzhi did not accept them.
translations.idiomatic: Wanzhi did not accept them.

sentences.zh: 帝問其故，答曰：「今日之賜，恩華俱重，但蓍簪弊席，復不可遺，所以不敢當。」

translations.literal: The Emperor asked the reason; he replied: "Today's gift—favor and splendor together are weighty; but worn rush hairpin and broken mat cannot be discarded, so I dare not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked the reason; he replied, "Today's gift—favor and splendor together are weighty; but worn rush hairpin and broken mat cannot be discarded, so I dare not accept.

sentences.zh: 帝善之。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 拜驃騎諮議參軍。

translations.literal: He was appointed Valiant Cavalry Adviser.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Valiant Cavalry Adviser.

sentences.zh: 霸府初開，賓客輻湊，高帝留意簡接。

translations.literal: When the Hegemon's headquarters first opened, guests gathered in crowds; the Emperor Gao paid attention to selective reception.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hegemon's headquarters first opened, guests gathered in crowds; Emperor Gao paid attention to selective reception.

sentences.zh: 玩之與樂安任遐俱以應對有席上之美，齊名見遇。

translations.literal: Wanzhi and Ren Xia of Le'an together had beauty in banquet repartee and were equally famed and favored.
translations.idiomatic: Wanzhi and Ren Xia of Le'an together had beauty in banquet repartee and were equally famed and favored.

sentences.zh: 玩之遷黃門郎。

translations.literal: Wanzhi was transferred to Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Wanzhi was transferred to Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 富陽人唐宇之僑居桐廬，父祖相傳圖墓為業。

translations.literal: Tang Yuzhi of Fuyang, sojourning in Tonglu, had fathers and grandfathers who transmitted tomb-mapping as their trade.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Yuzhi of Fuyang, sojourning in Tonglu, had fathers and grandfathers who transmitted tomb-mapping as their trade.

sentences.zh: 宇之自云其家墓有王氣。

translations.literal: Yuzhi himself said his family tomb had kingly qi.
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhi himself said his family tomb had kingly qi.

sentences.zh: 山中得金印，轉相誑惑。

translations.literal: In the mountains he obtained a gold seal and turned to deceiving others.
translations.idiomatic: In the mountains he obtained a gold seal and turned to deceiving others.

sentences.zh: 永明二年冬，宇之聚黨，遂陷富陽。

translations.literal: In winter of the second year of Yongming, Yuzhi gathered a party and thereupon seized Fuyang.
translations.idiomatic: In winter of the second year of Yongming, Yuzhi gathered a party and thereupon seized Fuyang.

sentences.zh: 至錢唐僭號，置太子。

translations.literal: Reaching Qiantang he usurped a title and established a crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Qiantang he usurped a title and established a crown prince.

sentences.zh: 賊遂據郡，又遣偽會稽太守孫泓取山陰。

translations.literal: The bandits then held the commandery and also sent a false Kuaiji Prefect Sun Hong to take Shanyin.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits then held the commandery and also sent a false Kuaiji Prefect Sun Hong to take Shanyin.

sentences.zh: 時會稽太守王敬則朝正，故宇之謂可乘虛而襲。

translations.literal: At that time Kuaiji Prefect Wang Jingze was at court for the regular audience, so Yuzhi thought he could take advantage of the vacancy to attack.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Kuaiji Prefect Wang Jingze was at court for the regular audience, so Yuzhi thought he could take advantage of the vacancy to attack.

sentences.zh: 泓至浦陽江，而郡丞張思祖遣浹口戍主楊休武拒戰，大破之。

translations.literal: Hong reached the Puyang River; the commandery aide Zhang Sinzu sent Xiakou garrison master Yang Xiuwu to resist; he was greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Hong reached the Puyang River; the commandery aide Zhang Sinzu sent Xiakou garrison master Yang Xiuwu to resist; he was greatly defeated.

sentences.zh: 朝廷遣禁兵東討，至錢唐，一戰便散，禽斬宇之。

translations.literal: The court sent forbidden troops east to attack; reaching Qiantang, one battle and they scattered; Yuzhi was captured and executed.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent forbidden troops east to attack; reaching Qiantang, one battle and they scattered; Yuzhi was captured and executed.

sentences.zh: 進兵平諸郡縣，台軍乘勝，百姓頗被強奪。

translations.literal: Advancing troops pacified the commanderies and counties; the capital army rode victory and the common people suffered much forcible seizure.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing troops pacified the commanderies and counties; the capital army rode victory and the common people suffered much forcible seizure.

sentences.zh: 軍還，上聞之，收軍主、前軍將軍陳天福棄市。

translations.literal: When the army returned the sovereign heard of it and had army master and former Vanguard General Chen Tianfu executed in the market.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned the sovereign heard of it and had army master and former Vanguard General Chen Tianfu executed in the market.

sentences.zh: 天福善馬矟，為諸將法，上寵將也。

translations.literal: Tianfu was skilled with the horse lance and was the model for all generals; the sovereign favored generals.
translations.idiomatic: Tianfu was skilled with the horse lance and was the model for all generals; the sovereign favored generals.

sentences.zh: 既伏誅，內外莫不震肅。

translations.literal: Once he was executed, inside and outside none did not tremble in awe.
translations.idiomatic: Once he was executed, inside and outside none did not tremble in awe.

sentences.zh: 玩之以久宦衰疾，上表告退，許之。

translations.literal: Wanzhi, because of long service, decline, and illness, submitted a memorial asking to retire; it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Wanzhi, because of long service, decline, and illness, submitted a memorial asking to retire; it was granted.

sentences.zh: 玩之于人物好臧否，宋末，王儉舉員外郎孔魁使魏，玩之言論不相饒，逖、儉並恨之。

translations.literal: Wanzhi in judging people was good at praise and blame; at the end of Song, Wang Jian recommended Staff Member Kong Kui to go to Wei; Wanzhi's remarks were not mutually forgiving—Xia and Jian both resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Wanzhi in judging people was good at praise and blame; at the end of Song, Wang Jian recommended Staff Member Kong Kui to go to Wei; Wanzhi's remarks were not mutually forgiving—Xia and Jian both resented him.

sentences.zh: 至是，玩之東歸，儉不出送，朝廷無祖餞者。

translations.literal: By then Wanzhi returned east; Jian did not come out to see him off; the court had no farewell feast.
translations.idiomatic: By then Wanzhi returned east; Jian did not come out to see him off; the court had no farewell feast.

sentences.zh: 中丞劉休與親知書曰：「虞公散發海隅，同古人之美，而東都之送，殊不藹藹。」

translations.literal: Censor Liu Xiu wrote to kin and friends: "Lord Yu has scattered his hair at the sea's edge, sharing the ancients' beauty—but the eastern capital's send-off was far from harmonious."
translations.idiomatic: Censor Liu Xiu wrote to kin and friends, "Lord Yu has scattered his hair at the sea's edge, sharing the ancients' beauty—but the eastern capital's send-off was far from harmonious."

sentences.zh: 玩之歸家數年卒，其後員外郎孔瑄就儉求會稽五官。

translations.literal: Wanzhi returned home and died several years later; afterward Staff Member Kong Xuan asked Jian for Kuaiji Five-Officials.
translations.idiomatic: Wanzhi returned home and died several years later; afterward Staff Member Kong Xuan asked Jian for Kuaiji Five-Officials.

sentences.zh: 儉方盥，投皁莢於地曰：「卿鄉俗惡，虞玩之至死煩人。」

translations.literal: Jian was washing his face and threw the soap pod on the ground saying: "Your native customs are vile—Yu Wanzhi troubled people to his death."
translations.idiomatic: Jian was washing his face and threw the soap pod on the ground saying, "Your native customs are vile—Yu Wanzhi troubled people to his death."

sentences.zh: 劉休字弘明，沛郡相人也。

translations.literal: Liu Xiu, style name Hongming, was a man of Xiang in Pei Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiu, style name Hongming, was from Xiang in Pei Commandery.

sentences.zh: 初為駙馬都尉，宋明帝居藩，休為湘東國常侍，不為帝所知。

translations.literal: Initially he was Commandant of the Horse Guards; when Emperor Ming of Song was in a princely residence, Xiu was Xiangdong Kingdom Regular Attendant—not known to the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Initially he was Commandant of the Horse Guards; when Emperor Ming of Song was in a princely residence, Xiu was Xiangdong Kingdom Regular Attendant—not known to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 襲祖封南鄉侯。

translations.literal: He inherited his grandfather's enfeoffment as Marquis of Nanxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited his grandfather's enfeoffment as Marquis of Nanxiang.

sentences.zh: 友人陳郡謝儼同丞相義宣反，休坐匿之，被系尚方。

translations.literal: His friend Xie Yan of Chen Commandery joined Chancellor Yixuan in rebellion; Xiu was implicated for hiding him and was detained in the Palace Workshops.
translations.idiomatic: His friend Xie Yan of Chen Commandery joined Chancellor Yixuan in rebellion; Xiu was implicated for hiding him and was detained in the Palace Workshops.

sentences.zh: 孝武崩乃得出。

translations.literal: Only when Emperor Xiaowu died was he able to come out.
translations.idiomatic: Only when Emperor Xiaowu died was he able to come out.

sentences.zh: 泰始初，諸州反，休素能筮，知明帝當勝，靜處不預異謀。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taishi, when the provinces rebelled, Xiu was skilled at divination and knew the Emperor Ming would prevail; he stayed quiet and did not join the plot.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Taishi, when the provinces rebelled, Xiu was skilled at divination and knew Emperor Ming would prevail; he stayed quiet and did not join the plot.

sentences.zh: 休之系尚方也，尚方令吳喜愛其才，後投吳喜，為喜輔師府錄事參軍。

translations.literal: When Xiu was detained in the Palace Workshops, the Palace Workshops Director Wu Xi loved his talent; later he went to Wu Xi and became Xi's Assistant Master of Records.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiu was detained in the Palace Workshops, the Palace Workshops Director Wu Xi loved his talent; later he went to Wu Xi and became Xi's Assistant Master of Records.

sentences.zh: 喜進之明帝，得在左右，板桂陽王征北參軍。

translations.literal: Xi introduced him to Emperor Ming and he gained a place at his side; he was appointed Guiyang Prince's Northern Expedition Staff Officer.
translations.idiomatic: Xi introduced him to Emperor Ming and he gained a place at his side; he was appointed Guiyang Prince's Northern Expedition Staff Officer.

sentences.zh: 帝頗有好尚，尤嗜飲食。

translations.literal: The Emperor had many preferences and especially loved food and drink.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had many preferences and especially loved food and drink.

sentences.zh: 休多藝能，爰至鼎味，莫不閑解，遂見親賞，長直殿內。

translations.literal: Xiu had many arts and skills, down to cauldron flavors—all he understood well; he was then met with intimate favor and long served inside the halls.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu had many arts and skills, down to cauldron flavors—all he understood well; he was then met with intimate favor and long served inside the halls.

sentences.zh: 後宮孕者，帝使筮其男女，無不如占。

translations.literal: When women in the rear palace were pregnant the Emperor had Xiu divine male or female—none failed to match the divination.
translations.idiomatic: When women in the rear palace were pregnant the emperor had Xiu divine male or female—none failed to match the divination.

sentences.zh: 帝憎婦人妒，尚書右丞勞彥遠以善棋見親，婦妒傷其面，帝曰：「我為卿斷之，何如？」

translations.literal: The Emperor hated jealous wives; Right Assistant Minister Lao Yanyuan was met with favor for skill at chess; his wife's jealousy injured his face; the Emperor said: "I shall cut it off for you—how about that?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor hated jealous wives; Right Assistant Minister Lao Yanyuan was met with favor for skill at chess; his wife's jealousy injured his face; the emperor said, "I shall cut it off for you—how about that?

sentences.zh: 彥遠率爾從旨。

translations.literal: Yanyuan rashly followed the intent.
translations.idiomatic: Yanyuan rashly followed the intent.

sentences.zh: 其夕，遂賜藥殺其妻。

translations.literal: That evening he was bestowed medicine and his wife was killed.
translations.idiomatic: That evening he was bestowed medicine and his wife was killed.

sentences.zh: 休妻王氏亦妒，帝聞之，賜休妾，敕與王氏二十杖。

translations.literal: Xiu's wife the Lady Wang was also jealous; the Emperor heard of it, bestowed Xiu a concubine, and ordered twenty strokes for the Lady Wang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu's wife the Lady Wang was also jealous; the emperor heard of it, bestowed Xiu a concubine, and ordered twenty strokes for the Lady Wang.

sentences.zh: 令休於宅後開小店，使王氏親賣皁莢掃帚，以此辱之。

translations.literal: He ordered Xiu to open a small shop behind his residence and had the Lady Wang personally sell soap pods and brooms, thereby humiliating her.
translations.idiomatic: He had Xiu open a small shop behind his house and made Lady Wang sell soap pods and brooms herself, to humiliate her.

sentences.zh: 其見親如此。

translations.literal: This was how he was treated with intimacy.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the favor shown him.

sentences.zh: 尋除員外郎，領輔國司馬，中書通事舍人，帶南城令。

translations.literal: Soon he was dismissed as Staff Member, leading Pacify-the-State Staff Major, Secretariat Communication Gentleman, and concurrently Magistrate of Nancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was Staff Member, leading Pacify-the-State Staff Major, Secretariat Communication Gentleman, and concurrently Magistrate of Nancheng.

sentences.zh: 後為都水使者，南康相。

translations.literal: Later he was Commissioner of Waterways and Xiang of Nankang.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was Commissioner of Waterways and prefect of Nankang.

sentences.zh: 善談政體，而在郡無異績。

translations.literal: He was skilled at discussing government institutions, yet in the commandery had no special achievements.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at discussing government institutions, yet in the commandery achieved nothing notable.

sentences.zh: 齊建元初，為御史中丞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qi Jianyuan he was Censor.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Qi Jianyuan he was Censor.

sentences.zh: 頃之啟言：「宋世載祀六十，曆斯任者五十有三，校其年月，不過盈歲。

translations.literal: Before long he memorialized: "The Song dynasty bore the sacrifice sixty years; those who held this post numbered fifty-three; comparing their years and months, none exceeded a full year.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he memorialized, "Song bore the sacrifice for sixty years; fifty-three men held this post, and none served more than a year on average.

sentences.zh: 於臣叨濫，宜請骸骨。」

translations.literal: As for your subject's presumptuous excess, I ought to request my old bones.
translations.idiomatic: I have overstayed my welcome and ought to request retirement.

sentences.zh: 四年，出為豫章內史，卒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he went out as Yuzhang Internal Administrator and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he went out as Yuzhang Internal Administrator and died.

sentences.zh: 宋末，造指南車，高帝以休有思理，使與王僧虔對共監試。

translations.literal: At the end of Song he constructed a south-pointing carriage; the Emperor Gao, because Xiu had thoughtful principle, had him jointly supervise trials with Wang Sengqian.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Song he constructed a south-pointing carriage; Emperor Gao, finding Xiu thoughtful, had him jointly supervise trials with Wang Sengqian.

sentences.zh: 又元嘉中，羊欣重王子敬正隸書，世共宗之，右軍之體微輕，不復見貴。

translations.literal: Also in Yuanjia, Yang Xin valued Wang Zijing's regular clerical script and the age together took it as standard; the Right General's style was slightly light and no longer prized.
translations.idiomatic: Also in Yuanjia, Yang Xin prized Wang Zijing's regular clerical script and the age took it as standard; Wang Xizhi's style grew slightly light and fell from favor.

sentences.zh: 及休始好右軍法，因此大行云。

translations.literal: When Xiu first favored the Right General's method, it thereby spread widely.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiu first favored Wang Xizhi's method, it spread widely.

sentences.zh: 江祏字弘業，濟陽考城人也。

translations.literal: Jiang Shi, style name Hongye, was a man of Kaocheng in Jiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Shi, style name Hongye, was from Kaocheng in Jiyang.

sentences.zh: 祖遵，寧朔參軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zun was Pacify-the-North Staff Officer.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zun was Pacify-the-North Staff Officer.

sentences.zh: 父德驎，司徒右長史。

translations.literal: His father Delin was Secretariat Right Senior Recorder.
translations.idiomatic: His father Delin was Secretariat Right Senior Recorder.

sentences.zh: 祏姑為齊高帝兄始安貞王道生妃，追諡景皇后，生齊明帝。

translations.literal: Shi's paternal aunt was consort to the Qi Emperor Gao's elder brother, Prince Zhen of Shi'an, Daosheng; posthumously titled Empress Jing; she bore the Qi Emperor Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Shi's paternal aunt was consort to Emperor Gao of Qi's elder brother, Prince Daosheng of Shi'an; posthumously titled Empress Jing; she bore Emperor Ming of Qi.

sentences.zh: 祏少為明帝所親，恩如兄弟。

translations.literal: Shi from youth was intimate with Emperor Ming; favor like brothers.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Shi was intimate with Emperor Ming; their bond was like brothers.

sentences.zh: 明帝為吳興，以祏為郡丞。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming was in Wuxing, he took Shi as commandery aide.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming held Wuxing, he made Shi commandery aide.

sentences.zh: 後除通直郎，補南徐州別駕。

translations.literal: Later he was dismissed as Direct Transmission Lang and supplemented as Nan Xuzhou Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was Direct Transmission Lang and supplemented as Nan Xuzhou Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 明帝輔政，委以腹心，引為驃騎諮議參軍，領南平昌太守。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming assisted in government he entrusted him with innermost trust, drew him in as Valiant Cavalry Adviser, and led Nan Pingchang Prefect.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming assisted in government he entrusted him with innermost trust, drew him in as Valiant Cavalry Adviser, and led Nan Pingchang Prefect.

sentences.zh: 時新立海陵，人情未服，祏每說明帝以君臣大節，明帝轉顧而不言。

translations.literal: At that time the newly established Prince of Hailing—popular feeling did not submit; Shi often spoke to Emperor Ming on the great integrity of ruler and minister; Emperor Ming turned to look but said nothing.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the newly established Prince of Hailing had not won popular assent; Shi often spoke to Emperor Ming on the great integrity of ruler and minister; Emperor Ming turned away and said nothing.

sentences.zh: 明帝胛上有赤志，常秘不傳，既而祏勸帝出以示人。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming had a red mole on his shoulder blade, always kept secret and not transmitted; afterward Shi urged the Emperor to show it to people.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming had a red mole on his shoulder blade, always kept secret; afterward Shi urged him to show it to people.

sentences.zh: 晉壽太守王洪范罷任還，上袒示之曰：「人皆謂此是日月相，卿幸無泄之。」

translations.literal: Jinshou Prefect Wang Hongfan finished his term and returned; the sovereign bared himself to show him and said: "All say this is a sun-and-moon mark—you must not leak it.
translations.idiomatic: Jinshou Prefect Wang Hongfan finished his term and returned; the sovereign bared himself and said, "All say this is a sun-and-moon mark—you must not leak it.

sentences.zh: 洪範曰：「公日月在軀，如何可隱？

translations.literal: Hongfan said: "Your Grace's sun and moon are on your body—how can they be hidden?
translations.idiomatic: Hongfan said, "Your Grace's sun and moon are on your body—how can they be hidden?

sentences.zh: 轉當言之公卿。」

translations.literal: I ought to speak of it to the dukes and ministers.
translations.idiomatic: I ought to speak of it to the dukes and ministers.

sentences.zh: 上大悅。

translations.literal: The sovereign was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 會直後張伯、尹瓚等屢謀竊發，祏憂虞無計，每夕輒托事外出。

translations.literal: Attendant-after Zhang Bo, Yin Zan, and others repeatedly plotted secret outbreaks; Shi, anxious without plan, every evening pretended business and went out.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant-after Zhang Bo, Yin Zan, and others repeatedly plotted secret outbreaks; Shi, anxious and without a plan, every evening pretended business and went out.

sentences.zh: 及明帝入纂議定，加祏甯朔將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming entered to succeed and the matter was settled, Shi was given added Pacify-the-North General.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming entered to succeed and the matter was settled, Shi was given added Pacify-the-North General.

sentences.zh: 帝失德既彰，祏議欲立江夏王寶玄。

translations.literal: The Emperor's loss of virtue was already manifest; Shi discussed wishing to establish the Prince of Jiangxia, Baoxuan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's loss of virtue was already manifest; Shi discussed wishing to establish Prince Baoxuan of Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 劉暄初為寶玄郢州行事，執事過刻。

translations.literal: Liu Xuan initially was Baoxuan's Yingzhou acting officer; his handling of affairs was overly harsh.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xuan initially was Baoxuan's Yingzhou acting officer; his handling of affairs was overly harsh.

sentences.zh: 有人獻馬，寶玄欲看之，暄曰：「馬何用看。」

translations.literal: Someone presented a horse; Baoxuan wished to look at it; Xuan said: "What use is looking at a horse?
translations.idiomatic: Someone presented a horse; Baoxuan wished to look at it; Xuan said, "What use is looking at a horse?

sentences.zh: 妃索煮肫，帳下諮暄，暄曰：「旦已煮鵝，不煩復此。」

translations.literal: The consort asked for boiled tripe; the tent staff consulted Xuan; Xuan said: "This morning goose was already boiled—no need for this again."
translations.idiomatic: The consort asked for boiled tripe; the tent staff consulted Xuan; Xuan said, "This morning goose was already boiled—no need for this again."

sentences.zh: 寶玄恚曰：「舅殊無渭陽之情。」

translations.literal: Baoxuan angrily said: "Uncle utterly lacks Wei-yang affection."
translations.idiomatic: Baoxuan angrily said, "Uncle utterly lacks Wei-yang affection."

sentences.zh: 暄聞之亦不悅。

translations.literal: Xuan heard this and was also displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan heard this and was also displeased.

sentences.zh: 至是不同祏議，欲立建安王寶寅。

translations.literal: By then he differed from Shi's plan and wished to establish the Prince of Jian'an, Baoyin.
translations.idiomatic: By then he differed from Shi's plan and wished to establish Prince Baoyin of Jian'an.

sentences.zh: 密謀於遙光，遙光自以年長，屬當鼎命，微旨動祏。

translations.literal: He secretly plotted with Yaoguang; Yaoguang, considering himself older and due the mandate, subtly moved Shi.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly plotted with Yaoguang; Yaoguang, considering himself older and due the mandate, subtly moved Shi.

sentences.zh: 祏弟祀以少主難保，勸祏立遙光。

translations.literal: Shi's younger brother Si, because the young sovereign was hard to preserve, urged Shi to establish Yaoguang.
translations.idiomatic: Shi's younger brother Si, because the young sovereign was hard to preserve, urged Shi to establish Yaoguang.

sentences.zh: 暄以遙光若立，己失元舅之望，不肯同。

translations.literal: Xuan, if Yaoguang were established, would himself lose hope as chief maternal uncle and would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan, if Yaoguang were established, would himself lose hope as chief maternal uncle and would not agree.

sentences.zh: 故祏遲疑久不決。

translations.literal: Therefore Shi hesitated long without deciding.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Shi hesitated long without deciding.

sentences.zh: 遙光大怒，遣左右黃曇慶於青溪橋道中刺殺暄。

translations.literal: Yaoguang was greatly enraged and sent his attendant Huang Tanqing on the road at Qingxi Bridge to assassinate Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yaoguang was greatly enraged and sent his attendant Huang Tanqing on the road at Qingxi Bridge to assassinate Xuan.

sentences.zh: 曇慶見暄部伍人多，不敢發。

translations.literal: Tanqing saw Xuan's retinue was numerous and did not dare strike.
translations.idiomatic: Tanqing saw Xuan's retinue was numerous and did not dare strike.

sentences.zh: 事覺，暄告祏謀，帝處分收祏兄弟。

translations.literal: The affair was exposed; Xuan informed on Shi's plot; the Emperor disposed to arrest the Shi brothers.
translations.idiomatic: The affair was exposed; Xuan informed on Shi's plot; the emperor disposed to arrest the Shi brothers.

sentences.zh: 祀時直在殿內，疑有異，遣信報祏曰：「劉暄似有謀，今作何計？」

translations.literal: Si at that time was on duty inside the hall, suspected something amiss, sent word to Shi: "Liu Xuan seems to have a plot—what plan now?
translations.idiomatic: Si at that time was on duty inside the hall, suspected something amiss, sent word to Shi, "Liu Xuan seems to have a plot—what plan now?

sentences.zh: 祏曰：「政當靜以鎮之。」

translations.literal: Shi said: "We should just calm and suppress it."
translations.idiomatic: Shi said, "We should just calm and suppress it."

sentences.zh: 俄而召祏入見，停中書省。

translations.literal: Before long Shi was summoned to audience and detained in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Shi was summoned to audience and detained in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 先是，直齋袁文曠以王敬則勳當封，祏執不與。

translations.literal: Earlier, Direct Attendant Yuan Wenkuan, because Wang Jingze's merit should be enfeoffed, Shi held and would not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Direct Attendant Yuan Wenkuan, because Wang Jingze's merit should be enfeoffed, Shi held and would not grant it.

sentences.zh: 帝使文曠取祏，以刀環築其心，曰：「復能奪我封不？」

translations.literal: The Emperor sent Wenkuan to take Shi; with the knife-ring he struck his heart and said: "Can you again seize my enfeoffment?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Wenkuan to take Shi; with the knife-ring he struck his heart and said, "Can you again seize my enfeoffment?

sentences.zh: 祏、祀同日見殺。

translations.literal: Shi and Si were killed the same day.
translations.idiomatic: Shi and Si were killed the same day.

sentences.zh: 祏任寄雖重，而不忘財利，論者以此少之。

translations.literal: Though Shi's trust was weighty, he did not forget wealth and profit; commentators for this thought slightly less of him.
translations.idiomatic: Though Shi's trust was weighty, he did not forget wealth and profit; commentators for this thought slightly less of him.

sentences.zh: 祏等既誅，帝恣意遊走，單騎賓士，謂左右曰：「祏常禁吾騎馬，小子若在，吾豈能得此。」

translations.literal: Once Shi and the rest were executed, the Emperor roamed at will, alone on horseback with guests; he said to attendants: "Shi always forbade my riding horses—if the boy were still here, how could I get this?
translations.idiomatic: Once Shi and the rest were executed, the emperor roamed at will, alone on horseback with guests; he said to attendants, "Shi always forbade my riding horses—if the boy were still here, how could I get this?

sentences.zh: 因問祏親親餘誰，答曰：「江祥今猶在冶。」

translations.literal: He thereupon asked who among Shi's kin remained; the reply: "Jiang Xiang is still at Ye."
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon asked who among Shi's kin remained; the reply, "Jiang Xiang is still at Ye."

sentences.zh: 乃於馬上作敕，賜祥死。

translations.literal: He then on horseback composed an edict and granted Xiang death.
translations.idiomatic: He then on horseback composed an edict and granted Xiang death.

sentences.zh: 祀字景昌，歷位晉安王鎮北長史，南東海太守，行府州事。

translations.literal: Si, style name Jingchang, successively held posts as Jin'an Prince's Pacify-the-North Senior Recorder, Nan Donghai Prefect, and acting headquarters and province affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Si, style name Jingchang, successively held Jin'an Prince's Pacify-the-North Senior Recorder, Nan Donghai Prefect, and acting headquarters and province affairs.

sentences.zh: 祀弟禧，早卒。

translations.literal: Shi's younger brother Xi died early.
translations.idiomatic: Shi's younger brother Xi died early.

sentences.zh: 有子廞字偉卿，年十二，聞收至，謂家人曰：「伯既如此，無心獨存。」

translations.literal: He had a son Yin, style name Weiqing, age twelve; hearing the arrest had come, he told the family: "Uncle is already thus—I have no heart to live alone.
translations.idiomatic: He had a son Yin, style name Weiqing, age twelve; hearing the arrest had come, he told the family, "Uncle is already thus—I have no heart to live alone.

sentences.zh: 赴井死。

translations.literal: He threw himself into a well and died.
translations.idiomatic: He threw himself into a well and died.

sentences.zh: 劉暄字士穆，彭城人。

translations.literal: Liu Xuan, style name Shimu, was a man of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xuan, style name Shimu, was from Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 及聞祏等戮，眠中大驚，投出戶外。

translations.literal: When he heard Shi and the rest were executed, in sleep he was greatly startled and threw himself outside the door.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard Shi and the rest were executed, in sleep he was greatly startled and threw himself outside the door.

sentences.zh: 問左右：「收至未？」

translations.literal: He asked attendants: "Has the arrest come yet?
translations.idiomatic: He asked attendants, "Has the arrest come yet?

sentences.zh: 良久意定，還坐，大悲曰：「不念江，行自痛也。」

translations.literal: After long while his mind settled; he returned to sit and greatly grieved: "I did not think of Jiang—I bring pain on myself."
translations.idiomatic: After a long while his mind settled; he returned to sit and greatly grieved, "I did not think of Jiang—I bring pain on myself."

sentences.zh: 遙光事起，以討暄為名。

translations.literal: When Yaoguang's affair arose, he took attacking Xuan as the name.
translations.idiomatic: When Yaoguang's affair arose, he took attacking Xuan as the name.

sentences.zh: 事平，暄遷領軍將軍，封平都縣侯。

translations.literal: When the affair was pacified, Xuan was transferred to Defender-in-Chief and enfeoffed as Marquis of Pingdu.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was pacified, Xuan was transferred to Defender-in-Chief and enfeoffed as Marquis of Pingdu.

sentences.zh: 其年，茹法珍、梅蟲兒、徐世標譖暄有異志。

translations.literal: That year, Ru Fazhen, Mei Chong'er, and Xu Shibiao slandered Xuan as having different intent.
translations.idiomatic: That year, Ru Fazhen, Mei Chong'er, and Xu Shibiao slandered Xuan as having different intent.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「領軍是我舅，豈應有此？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "The Defender-in-Chief is my maternal uncle—how could he have this?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The Defender-in-Chief is my maternal uncle—how could he have this?

sentences.zh: 世標曰：「明帝是武帝同堂，恩遇如此，尚滅害都盡，舅復焉可信。」

translations.literal: Shibiao said: "Emperor Ming was Emperor Wu's same hall and was met with such favor—yet he destroyed the clan entirely; how can a maternal uncle again be trusted?"
translations.idiomatic: Shibiao said, "Emperor Ming was Emperor Wu's same hall and was met with such favor—yet he destroyed the clan entirely; how can a maternal uncle again be trusted?"

sentences.zh: 乃誅之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he was executed.

sentences.zh: 暄為人性軟弱，當軸居政，每事讓江祏，群弟不得進官。

translations.literal: Xuan's nature was soft and weak; holding the axis in government, in each matter he yielded to Jiang Shi; his brothers could not advance in office.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan's nature was soft and weak; holding the axis in government, in each matter he yielded to Jiang Shi; his brothers could not advance in office.

sentences.zh: 死之日，皆怨之。

translations.literal: On the day of death all resented him.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of death all resented him.

sentences.zh: 論曰：「君老不事太子」，義烈之遺訓也，欲夫專心所奉，在節無二。

translations.literal: The Discussion says: "When the lord is old, do not serve the crown prince"—this is the righteous teaching of martyrs' legacy; one wishes that single-minded devotion to what is upheld have integrity without duality.
translations.idiomatic: The Discussion says, "When the lord is old, do not serve the crown prince"—this is the righteous teaching of martyrs' legacy; one wishes that single-minded devotion to what is upheld have integrity without duality.

sentences.zh: 伯玉始遵其事，旋及誅夷，有以驗「行之惟艱」，且知齊武之非弘量矣。

translations.literal: Boyu first followed this matter, then swiftly met execution and extinction—thereby verifying that "action is hard"; and one knows the Qi Emperor Wu was not of broad measure.
translations.idiomatic: Boyu first followed this matter, then swiftly met execution and extinction—thereby verifying that "action is hard"; and one knows Emperor Wu of Qi was not of broad measure.

sentences.zh: 高帝作牧淮、兗，將興霸業，崔、蘇睹微知著，自同奔走。

translations.literal: When the Emperor Gao was governor of Huai and Yan, about to raise the hegemonic enterprise, Cui and Su saw the subtle and knew what was coming, themselves like running in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gao was governor of Huai and Yan, about to raise the hegemonic enterprise, Cui and Su saw the subtle and knew what was coming, themselves like running in attendance.

sentences.zh: 虞悰笥餌之恩，諧之心腹之寄，並得攀光日月，亦各時運之所躋乎。

translations.literal: Yu Cong's basket-and-bait favor, Xie's entrustment of innermost heart, both could climb the sun and moon's light—also each the fortune of the times they ascended.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Cong's basket-and-bait favor, Xie's entrustment of innermost heart, both could climb the sun and moon's light—also each the fortune of the times they ascended.

sentences.zh: 玩之臧否之尤，著在懸車之日，是知嗣宗所誡，蓋亦遠有致乎。

translations.literal: Wanzhi's excess in praise and blame was manifest on the day he hung up his carriage—thus one knows the warning Zongsun gave perhaps also had far-reaching intent.
translations.idiomatic: Wanzhi's excess in praise and blame was manifest on the day he hung up his carriage—thus one knows the warning Zongsun gave perhaps also had far-reaching intent.

sentences.zh: 江祏立辟非時，竟蹈龍逄之血，「人之多僻」，蓋詩人所深懼也。

translations.literal: Jiang Shi's establishing the heir was not timely; in the end he trod Longfeng's blood—"how many are depraved"—perhaps what the poet deeply feared.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Shi's establishing the heir was not timely; in the end he trod Longfeng's blood—"how many are depraved"—perhaps what the poet deeply feared.
